title.raw: 卷八十一 列傳第六十九: 儒林上 Volume 81 Biographies 69: Confucian Scholars 1

sentences.zh: 儒林上

translations.literal: Confucian Forest, Upper
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars, Part 1

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十九儒林上

translations.literal: Biographies Number Sixty-Nine: Confucian Forest Upper
translations.idiomatic: Biography 69: Confucian Scholars, Part 1

sentences.zh: 梁越盧醜張偉梁祚平恆陳奇劉獻之張吾貴劉蘭孫惠蔚族曾孫靈暉馬子結石曜靈暉子萬壽徐遵明董徵李業興子崇祖李鉉馮偉張買奴劉軌思鮑季詳邢峙劉晝馬敬德子元熙張景仁權會張思伯張雕武郭遵

translations.literal: Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Liu Xianzhi, Zhang Wugui, Liu Lan, Sun Huiwei and clan, great-grandson Linghui, Ma Zijie, Shi Yao, Linghui's son Wanshou, Xu Zunming, Dong Zheng, Li Yexing, son Chongzu, Li Xuan, Feng Wei, Zhang Mainu, Liu Guisi, Bao Jixiang, Xing Zhi, Liu Zhou, Ma Jingde, son Yuanxi, Zhang Jingren, Quan Hui, Zhang Sibo, Zhang Diaowu, Guo Zun
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Liu Xianzhi, Zhang Wugui, Liu Lan, Sun Huiwei and his clan, the great-grandson Linghui, Ma Zijie, Shi Yao, Linghui's son Wanshou, Xu Zunming, Dong Zheng, Li Yexing, his son Chongzu, Li Xuan, Feng Wei, Zhang Mainu, Liu Guisi, Bao Jixiang, Xing Zhi, Liu Zhou, Ma Jingde, his son Yuanxi, Zhang Jingren, Quan Hui, Zhang Sibo, Zhang Diaowu, and Guo Zun

sentences.zh: 儒者，其為教也大矣，其利物也博矣！

translations.literal: The Confucian, his teaching is great indeed, his benefiting things is broad indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of the Confucian school is vast in scope, and its benefits to the world are far-reaching!

sentences.zh: 以篤父子，以正君臣。

translations.literal: By it father and son are made sincere, by it ruler and minister are made correct.
translations.idiomatic: It strengthens the bond between father and son and sets right the relationship between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 開政化之本原，鑿生靈之耳目，百王損益，一以貫之。

translations.literal: It opens the root source of government and transformation, carves out the ears and eyes of living beings; the hundred kings' additions and subtractions all thread through on one strand.
translations.idiomatic: It lays open the foundations of governance and civilization and awakens the minds of the people; through all the changes wrought by successive dynasties, its thread runs unbroken.

sentences.zh: 雖世或汙隆，而斯文不墜。

translations.literal: Although the age may at times sink or rise, this culture does not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Though the times may decline or flourish, this tradition of learning has never been lost.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之後，宇內分崩，禮樂文章，掃地將盡。

translations.literal: From after the Yongjia era, within the four seas there was collapse and fragmentation; rites, music, and literature were swept to the ground and nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia reign, the realm fell apart, and ritual, music, and letters were all but swept away.

sentences.zh: 魏道武初定中原，雖日不暇給，始建都邑，便以經術為先。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu of Wei first settled the Central Plains, although each day allowed no respite, as soon as he began to establish capital cities, he took classical learning as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu of Wei first pacified the Central Plains, though pressed by daily affairs, he made classical studies a priority as soon as he began building his capitals.

sentences.zh: 立太學，置《五經》博士生員千有餘人。

translations.literal: He established the Imperial Academy and set up more than a thousand students for the Five Classics doctoral positions.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Imperial Academy and enrolled over a thousand students in the Five Classics doctoral program.

sentences.zh: 天興二年春，增國子太學生員至三千人。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Tianxing, he increased the Imperial Academy and National University students to three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Tianxing, enrollment at the National University and Imperial Academy was raised to three thousand students.

sentences.zh: 豈不以天下可馬上取之，不可以馬上臨之？

translations.literal: Was it not because the realm can be taken on horseback, but cannot be ruled from horseback?
translations.idiomatic: For did he not grasp that an empire may be won on horseback, but cannot be governed from the saddle?

sentences.zh: 聖達經猷，蓋為遠矣。

translations.literal: The sage's penetration of the classics' designs—how far-reaching it was!
translations.idiomatic: How far-sighted was this sage's understanding of the classics!

sentences.zh: 四年春，命樂師入學習舞，釋菜于先師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, he ordered music masters to enter the school to study dance and performed the vegetable-offering ceremony to the former masters.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, he had music masters enter the academy to learn ceremonial dance and offered vegetables in honor of the ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 明元時，改國子為中書學，立教授博士。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mingyuan, the National University was changed to the Directorate of Archives School, and teaching professors and doctors were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan, the National University was renamed the Directorate School, with professors and doctoral lecturers appointed.

sentences.zh: 太武始光三年春，起太學於城東。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Shiguang under Emperor Taiwu, the Imperial Academy was raised east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Shiguang under Emperor Taiwu, the Imperial Academy was built east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 後征盧玄、高允等，而令州郡各舉才學。

translations.literal: Later he summoned Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others, and ordered each province and commandery to recommend men of talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: He later summoned scholars such as Lu Xuan and Gao Yun and ordered each province and commandery to recommend men of learning and ability.

sentences.zh: 於是人多砥尚，儒術轉興。

translations.literal: Thereupon many people sharpened and esteemed learning, and Confucian arts turned and flourished.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, many took up the pursuit of learning, and Confucian scholarship began to flourish anew.

sentences.zh: 獻文天安初，詔立鄉學，郡置博士二人，助教二人，學生六十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an under Emperor Xianwen, an edict established village schools; each commandery was to have two doctors, two assistant teachers, and sixty students.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tian'an era under Emperor Xianwen, an edict established village schools, with each commandery assigned two doctors, two assistant teachers, and sixty students.

sentences.zh: 後詔大郡立博士二人，助教四人，學生一百人；

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered that large commanderies establish two doctors, four assistant teachers, and one hundred students;
translations.idiomatic: A later edict stipulated that large commanderies should have two doctors, four assistant teachers, and one hundred students;

sentences.zh: 次郡立博士二人，助教二人，學生八十人；

translations.literal: middle commanderies two doctors, two assistant teachers, and eighty students;
translations.idiomatic: medium commanderies two doctors, two assistant teachers, and eighty students;

sentences.zh: 中郡立博士一人，助教二人，學生六十人；

translations.literal: central commanderies one doctor, two assistant teachers, and sixty students;
translations.idiomatic: mid-sized commanderies one doctor, two assistant teachers, and sixty students;

sentences.zh: 下郡立博士一人，助教一人，學生四十人。

translations.literal: lower commanderies one doctor, one assistant teacher, and forty students.
translations.idiomatic: and smaller commanderies one doctor, one assistant teacher, and forty students.

sentences.zh: 太和中，改中書學為國子學，建明堂、辟雍，尊三老五更，又開皇子之學。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, the Directorate School was changed back to the National University; the Bright Hall and Imperial College were built; the Three Elders and Five More Venerable were honored; and furthermore the princes' school was opened.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, the Directorate School was restored as the National University; the Bright Hall and Imperial College were constructed; the Three Elders and Five More Venerable were honored; and schools for the imperial princes were established.

sentences.zh: 及遷都洛邑，詔立國子、太學、四門小學。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, an edict established the National University, Imperial Academy, and Four Gates Elementary School.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang, an edict founded the National University, the Imperial Academy, and the Four Gates Elementary School.

sentences.zh: 孝文欽明稽古，篤好墳籍，坐輿據鞍，不忘講道。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen admired clarity and investigated antiquity, ardently loved the classics in their tombs, and whether seated in a carriage or mounted on a saddle, did not forget to lecture on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was a keen student of antiquity who loved the classical texts devotedly; whether riding in his carriage or on horseback, he never ceased expounding the classics.

sentences.zh: 劉芳、李彪諸人以經書進，崔光、邢巒之徒以文史達。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, Li Biao, and others advanced through the classics; Cui Guang, Xing Luan, and their kind attained eminence through literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, Li Biao, and others rose through mastery of the classics, while Cui Guang, Xing Luan, and their peers gained prominence through letters and history.

sentences.zh: 其餘涉獵典章，閑集詞翰，莫不縻以好爵，動貽賞眷。

translations.literal: The rest who ranged through canonical regulations or leisurely gathered literary compositions—all without exception were tethered with fine ranks and constantly bestowed favor and regard.
translations.idiomatic: All others who dipped into the canon or excelled in literary composition were rewarded with fine offices and showered with imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 於是斯文郁然，比靈斯周、漢。

translations.literal: Thereupon this culture flourished luxuriantly, comparable in spirit to the Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Learning thus flourished abundantly, rivaling in splendor the great ages of Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，復詔營國學。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuanwu, an edict again ordered the construction of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, an edict again ordered the rebuilding of the National University.

sentences.zh: 樹小學於四門，大選儒生以為小學博士，員四十人。

translations.literal: An elementary school was planted at the Four Gates; a great selection of Confucian scholars was made to serve as elementary-school doctors, forty in number.
translations.idiomatic: An elementary school was established at the Four Gates, and forty eminent Confucian scholars were chosen as its doctoral lecturers.

sentences.zh: 雖黌宇未立，而經術彌顯。

translations.literal: Although the school buildings were not yet erected, classical learning grew ever more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Though the school buildings had not yet been completed, classical scholarship grew ever more prominent.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，學業大盛，故燕、齊、趙、魏之間，橫經著錄，不可勝數。

translations.literal: At that time the realm enjoyed peace, and scholarly pursuits greatly flourished; thus between Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei, those who stretched out the classics and were recorded could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace and scholarship thrived; throughout Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei, scholars with classics in hand and students on their rolls were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 大者千餘人，小者猶數百。

translations.literal: The large had more than a thousand persons; the small still had several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The largest schools had over a thousand students; even the smallest had several hundred.

sentences.zh: 州舉茂異，郡貢孝廉，對揚王庭，每年逾眾。

translations.literal: Provinces recommended outstanding and unusual men; commanderies presented filial and incorrupt candidates; they answered and displayed themselves at the royal court, and each year they exceeded the previous in number.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces nominated outstanding scholars, commanderies sent up filial and incorrupt candidates, and each year more thronged the imperial court for examination than the year before.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，將立國學，詔以三品以上，及五品清官之子以充生選。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era, when the National University was about to be established, an edict ordered that sons of officials of the third rank and above, and sons of fifth-rank pure officials, should fill the student selections.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era, as the National University was being planned, an edict stipulated that sons of third-rank officials and above, and sons of fifth-rank pure officials, should serve as student candidates.

sentences.zh: 未及簡置，仍復停寢。

translations.literal: Before selection and placement could be completed, it again ceased and lay dormant.
translations.idiomatic: Before selections could be made, the project was suspended once again.

sentences.zh: 正光三年，乃釋奠于國學，命祭酒崔光講《孝經》，始置國子生三十六人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang, the libation ceremony was finally performed at the National University; the libationer Cui Guang was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; and for the first time thirty-six National University students were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengguang, the libation ceremony was held at the National University; Libationer Cui Guang lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; and thirty-six National University students were enrolled for the first time.

sentences.zh: 暨孝昌之後，海內淆亂，四方校學，所存無幾。

translations.literal: After the Xiaochang era, within the seas there was turmoil and disorder; of the schools in all four directions, scarcely any survived.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiaochang era, the realm fell into chaos, and few schools anywhere survived.

sentences.zh: 齊神武生于邊朔，長於戎馬，杖義建旗，掃清區縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenwu of Qi was born on the northern frontier, grew up amid war-horses, leaned on righteousness to raise his banner, and swept clean the districts and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu of Qi was born on the northern frontier and reared in the saddle; rallying men under the banner of righteousness, he swept the realm clean of disorder.

sentences.zh: 因魏氏喪亂，屬爾硃殘酷，文章咸蕩，禮樂同奔，弦歌之音且絕，俎豆之容將盡。

translations.literal: Because the Wei house fell into disorder and at that time the Erzhu were cruel, literature was all swept away, rites and music fled together, the sound of string and song was about to cease, and the appearance of sacrificial vessels and stands was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of the dying Wei and the cruelty of the Erzhu clan, literature was destroyed, ritual and music fled together, the sound of stringed instruments and song all but died out, and the rites of sacrifice were nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，孝武復釋奠于國學，又于顯陽殿詔祭酒劉欽講《孝經》，黃門李鬱說《禮記》，中書舍人盧景宣講《大戴禮夏小正》篇，復置生七十二人。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, Emperor Xiaowu again performed the libation ceremony at the National University; furthermore at the Xianyang Hall he ordered Libationer Liu Qin to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen Li Yu to expound the Book of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan to lecture on the "Xiaozheng" chapter of the Elder Dai's Rites; and seventy-two students were again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, Emperor Xiaowu again held the libation ceremony at the National University; at the Xianyang Hall he had Libationer Liu Qin lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Li Yu of the Huangmen expound the Book of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan lecture on the "Xiaozheng" chapter of the Elder Dai's Rites; and seventy-two students were enrolled anew.

sentences.zh: 及永熙西遷，天平北徙，雖庠序之制，有所未遑，而儒雅之道，遽形心慮。

translations.literal: When Yongxi moved west and Tianping shifted north, although the system of schools had matters not yet attended to, the way of refined Confucian learning swiftly took shape in the mind's concerns.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved west at Yongxi and north at Tianping, though the school system could not yet be fully restored, the cause of refined learning swiftly took root in the rulers' minds.

sentences.zh: 時初遷都于鄴，國子置生三十六人。

translations.literal: At that time, when the capital was first moved to Ye, the National University appointed thirty-six students.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was first moved to Ye, thirty-six students were enrolled at the National University.

sentences.zh: 至興和、武定之間，儒業復盛矣。

translations.literal: By the time between Xinghe and Wuding, Confucian pursuits flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xinghe and Wuding eras, Confucian scholarship had flourished once more.

sentences.zh: 始天平中，范陽盧景裕同從兄仲禮于本郡起逆，齊神武免其罪，置之賓館，以經教授太原公以下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era, Lu Jingyu of Fanyang together with his paternal cousin Zhongli raised rebellion in their native commandery; Emperor Shenwu of Qi pardoned their crimes, placed them in the guest lodge, and had them teach the classics to the Prince of Taiyuan and those below.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianping era, Lu Jingyu of Fanyang and his cousin Zhongli rebelled in their home commandery; Emperor Shenwu pardoned them, lodged them as honored guests, and had them instruct the Prince of Taiyuan and his brothers in the classics.

sentences.zh: 及景裕卒，又以趙郡李同軌繼之。

translations.literal: When Jingyu died, Li Tonggui of Zhao commandery succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingyu's death, Li Tonggui of Zhao commandery took his place.

sentences.zh: 二賢並大蒙恩遇，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Both worthies greatly received favor and encounter, and were treated with exceptional ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Both men received extraordinary favor and were treated with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 同軌雲亡，復征中山張雕武、勃海李鉉、刁柔、中山石曜等遞為諸子師友。

translations.literal: When Tonggui passed away, Zhang Diaowu of Zhongshan, Li Xuan of Bohai, Diao Rou, Shi Yao of Zhongshan, and others were again summoned in turn to serve as teachers and friends to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: After Tonggui's death, Zhang Diaowu of Zhongshan, Li Xuan of Bohai, Diao Rou, Shi Yao of Zhongshan, and others were summoned in succession to serve as tutors to the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 及天保、大寧、武平之朝，亦引進名儒，授皇太子、諸王經術。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Tianbao, Daning, and Wuping as well, famous Confucians were also brought in to teach the classics to the crown prince and the various princes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianbao, Daning, and Wuping reigns as well, eminent Confucians were brought in to instruct the crown prince and the princes in the classics.

sentences.zh: 然爰自始基，暨于季世，唯濟南之在儲宮，性識聰敏，頗自砥礪，以成其美。

translations.literal: Yet from the beginning of the foundation down to the final age, only the Prince of Jinan while in the Eastern Palace was by nature intelligent and perceptive, and considerably polished himself to complete his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the founding of the dynasty to its decline, only the Prince of Jinan, while heir apparent, was naturally bright and diligent enough to cultivate his own excellence.

sentences.zh: 自餘多驕恣傲狠，動違禮度，日就月將，無聞焉爾。

translations.literal: The rest were mostly arrogant, willful, proud, and fierce; in movement they constantly violated ritual measure; day by day they approached and month by month they advanced—yet nothing was heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were mostly arrogant and unruly, constantly violating propriety; day after day they grew worse, yet nothing worthy was ever heard of them.

sentences.zh: 鏤冰雕朽，迄用無成，蓋有由焉。

translations.literal: Carving ice and sculpting rotten wood—ultimately there was no accomplishment; surely there were reasons for this.
translations.idiomatic: To carve ice or sculpt rotten wood is futile work—and there were good reasons why their schooling came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王子孫，習性驕逸。

translations.literal: Now the emperor's sons and grandsons by habit are proud and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons and grandsons are by nature proud and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 況義方之情不篤，邪僻之路競開，自非得自生知，體包上智。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the feeling of righteous direction is not sincere and devious paths compete to open, unless one is not born with innate knowledge and the body embraces supreme wisdom—
translations.idiomatic: When the moral guidance of their tutors is weak and devious paths beckon on every side, how could they succeed unless born with innate wisdom?

sentences.zh: 而內縱聲色之娛，外多犬馬之好，安能入則篤行，出則友賢者也？

translations.literal: yet within they indulge the pleasures of sound and color, and without they have many loves of dogs and horses—how could they at home practice sincere conduct and abroad befriend the worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they indulged pleasures within and pursued horses and hounds without—how could they practice virtue at home or seek out worthy companions abroad?

sentences.zh: 徒有師傅之資，終無琢磨之實。

translations.literal: They merely had the resources of masters and tutors; in the end there was no reality of polishing.
translations.idiomatic: They had tutors in name only, and in the end no real refinement took place.

sentences.zh: 貴遊之輩，飾以明經，可謂稽山竹箭，加之括羽，俯拾青紫，斷可知焉。

translations.literal: The class of noble wanderers adorned themselves with clarifying the classics—one might say bamboo arrows from Mount Ji, with feathered shafts added; stooping to pick up blue and purple, it could be known for certain.
translations.idiomatic: For the sons of the nobility, a show of classical learning was like fitting feathers to bamboo arrows from Mount Ji—official rank could be picked up at will, as surely as one could know.

sentences.zh: 而齊氏司存，或失其守；

translations.literal: Yet the Qi house's officers in charge sometimes lost their posts;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Qi dynasty the offices charged with education were sometimes left vacant;

sentences.zh: 師保疑丞，皆賞勳舊；

translations.literal: the masters, protectors, advisers, and assistants were all rewarded old meritorious men;
translations.idiomatic: tutors, protectors, advisers, and assistants were all appointed from among old meritocrats;

sentences.zh: 國學博士，徒有虛名。

translations.literal: the National University's doctors had only empty names.
translations.idiomatic: and the doctors of the National University held only empty titles.

sentences.zh: 唯國子一學，生徒數十人耳。

translations.literal: Only the one National University school had several tens of students, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Only the National University itself had a few dozen students at all.

sentences.zh: 胄子以通經進仕者，唯博陵崔子發、廣平宋遊卿而已。

translations.literal: Of imperial descendants who advanced to office through mastering the classics, there were only Cui Zifa of Boling and Song Youqing of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Of the imperial clansmen who rose through mastery of the classics, only Cui Zifa of Boling and Song Youqing of Guangping come to mind.

sentences.zh: 自外莫見其人。

translations.literal: Apart from these, no such persons were seen.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, none are known.

sentences.zh: 幸朝章寬簡，政綱疏闊，遊手浮惰，十室而九。

translations.literal: Fortunately the court regulations were lenient and simple, the governmental net sparse and broad; idlers and floating slackers were nine out of ten households.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately court regulations were lenient and governance loose; idlers and layabouts filled nine houses in ten.

sentences.zh: 故橫經受業之侶，遍於鄉邑；

translations.literal: Thus companions who stretched out the classics and received instruction were everywhere in villages and towns;
translations.idiomatic: Thus scholars with classics in hand were found in every village and town;

sentences.zh: 負笈從宦之徒，不遠千里。

translations.literal: those who bore satchels and followed teachers for office did not regard a thousand li as far.
translations.idiomatic: and students bearing satchels traveled a thousand li without hesitation to seek instruction.

sentences.zh: 入閭里之內，乞食為資，憩桑梓之陰，動逾十數。

translations.literal: Entering within lanes and hamlets, they begged food for sustenance; resting in the shade of their native mulberry trees, they often exceeded a dozen stops.
translations.idiomatic: They entered villages to beg for their meals and paused under hometown mulberry trees, often staying ten days or more at each stop.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙之俗，此眾尤甚焉。

translations.literal: In the customs of Yan and Zhao, this crowd was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: This was especially true in the regions of Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 齊制，諸郡並立學，置博士、助教授經。

translations.literal: Under Qi's regulations, all commanderies alike established schools, appointing doctors and assistants to teach the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi regulations, every commandery was to establish a school with doctors and assistants to teach the classics.

sentences.zh: 學生俱久差逼充員，士流及豪富之家，皆不從調。

translations.literal: Students were all long assigned by corvée to fill quotas; the gentry stream and wealthy powerful families all refused to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Students were conscripted by corvée to fill quotas, while gentry and wealthy families all refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 備員既非所好，墳籍固不開懷。

translations.literal: Filling quotas was not what they loved; the classics in their tombs certainly did not open their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Since filling quotas was not to their liking, they had no heart for the classical texts.

sentences.zh: 又多被州郡官人驅使，縱有遊惰，亦不檢察。

translations.literal: Moreover many were driven and used by provincial and commandery officials; even if they were idle and slack, no inspection was made.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many were pressed into service by local officials, and even the idle went unchecked.

sentences.zh: 皆由上非所好之所致也。

translations.literal: All were caused by those above not loving these things.
translations.idiomatic: All this stemmed from the rulers' own lack of interest in learning.

sentences.zh: 諸郡俱得察孝廉，其博士、助教及遊學之徒通經者，推擇充舉。

translations.literal: All commanderies alike could examine filial and incorrupt candidates; among their doctors, assistant teachers, and traveling students who had mastered the classics, the best were selected to fill the recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery could examine filial and incorrupt candidates, selecting from among its doctors, assistants, and traveling students those who had mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 射策十條，通八以上，聽九品出身，其尤異者，亦蒙抽擢。

translations.literal: In the target-shooting examination of ten questions, those who passed eight or more were permitted to enter office at the ninth rank; the especially outstanding also received special promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the written examination of ten questions, those who answered eight or more correctly were granted entry at the ninth rank, and the most outstanding were specially promoted.

sentences.zh: 周文受命，雅重經典。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou received the Mandate, he elegantly valued the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou received the Mandate, he held the classics in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 于時西都板蕩，戎馬生郊。

translations.literal: At that time the western capital was in upheaval; war-horses were born in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the western capital lay in ruins and war-horses grazed in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 先生之舊章，往聖之遺訓，掃地盡矣！

translations.literal: The former masters' old regulations, the past sages' handed-down instructions—all were swept to the ground and exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: The teachings of the ancient masters and the legacy of the sages had been swept utterly away!

sentences.zh: 於是求闕文于三古，得至理於千載，黜魏、晉之制度，復姬旦之茂典。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought missing texts in the Three Antiquities, obtained the ultimate principle from a thousand years, dismissed the Wei and Jin systems, and restored the Duke of Zhou's flourishing canon.
translations.idiomatic: He then sought lost texts from the three ancient dynasties, recovered timeless principles from a millennium of tradition, set aside Wei and Jin institutions, and restored the great rites of the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 盧景宣學通群藝，修五禮之缺；

translations.literal: Lu Jingxuan's learning penetrated all arts; he repaired the gaps in the Five Rites;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingxuan mastered every branch of learning and repaired the gaps in the Five Rites;

sentences.zh: 長孫紹遠才稱洽聞，正六樂之壞。

translations.literal: Changsun Shaoyuan's talent was called comprehensive knowledge; he corrected the ruin of the Six Music.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Shaoyuan was renowned for his breadth of knowledge and restored the corrupted Six Music.

sentences.zh: 由是朝章漸備，學者向風。

translations.literal: From this the court's regulations gradually became complete, and scholars turned toward the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Thus court ritual was gradually restored, and scholars flocked to the new order.

sentences.zh: 明皇纂曆，敦尚學藝，內有崇文之觀，外重成均之職。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming succeeded to the calendar, earnestly honored learning and arts; within there was the Palace of Venerating Literature, without the weight of the Imperial College's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne and promoted learning; within the palace he established the Hall of Venerating Literature, and without he strengthened the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 握素懷鉛，重席解頤之士，間出於朝廷；

translations.literal: Those who grasped plain silk and embraced the writing stylus, scholars of piled mats who loosened the chin in teaching, emerged from time to time at court;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who grasped brush and plain silk, masters whose layered seats drew eager listeners, appeared at court from time to time;

sentences.zh: 員冠方領，執經負笈之生，著錄於京邑。

translations.literal: round-capped and square-collared students who held the classics and bore satchels were recorded in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: and round-capped, square-collared students bearing classics and satchels enrolled in the capital.

sentences.zh: 濟濟焉，足以逾于向時矣。

translations.literal: Abundant and grand, it was sufficient to surpass former times.
translations.idiomatic: The scene was magnificent, surpassing anything seen in earlier days.

sentences.zh: 洎保定三年，帝乃下詔尊太保燕公為三老。

translations.literal: By the third year of Baoding, the emperor then issued an edict honoring the Grand Tutor, Duke of Yan, as one of the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding, the emperor issued an edict honoring the Grand Tutor, Duke of Yan, as one of the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 帝於是服兗冕，乘碧輅，陳文物，備禮容，清蹕而臨太學，袒割以食之，奉觴以酳之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon donned the dark cap and robes, rode the green carriage, arrayed cultural objects, prepared ritual demeanor, cleared the path with insignia and approached the Imperial Academy, bared his shoulder and cut meat to feed him, and raised the goblet to let him rinse his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then donned his ceremonial robes, rode in the green carriage, displayed the ritual regalia, and with full ceremony approached the Imperial Academy, where he bared his shoulder to cut meat for the Elder and raised a goblet for him to rinse his mouth.

sentences.zh: 斯固一世之盛事也。

translations.literal: This was indeed a grand event of an age.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly a grand occasion of the age.

sentences.zh: 其後命輶軒而致玉帛，征沈重于南荊。

translations.literal: Afterward he ordered the light carriage to go bearing jade and silk, and summoned the weighty and profound from the southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He later sent envoys bearing jade and silk to summon eminent scholars from the southern provinces.

sentences.zh: 及定山東，降至尊而勞萬乘，待熊安生以殊禮。

translations.literal: When Shandong was settled, he lowered the supreme honor to labor on behalf of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler, and treated Xiong Ansheng with exceptional ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Shandong, he humbled himself before the sage Xiong Ansheng and treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 是以天下慕向，文教遠覃。

translations.literal: Thus the realm admired and turned toward it; civil culture and teaching extended far.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm turned toward learning, and culture and education spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 衣儒者之服，挾先王之道，開黌舍，延學徒者比肩；

translations.literal: Those who wore the Confucian robe and embraced the former kings' Way, who opened schoolhouses and extended students, stood shoulder to shoulder;
translations.idiomatic: Men in scholars' robes who embraced the way of the ancient kings opened schools and took on students shoulder to shoulder;

sentences.zh: 勵從師之志，守專門炎業，辭親戚，甘勤苦者成市。

translations.literal: those who encouraged the will to follow teachers, who kept to a single specialty's blazing pursuit, who left kin and gladly bore hardship and toil, formed a market.
translations.idiomatic: those who steeled their resolve to study, devoted themselves to a single discipline, left home, and gladly endured hardship filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 雖通儒盛業，不逮魏、晉之臣，而風移俗變，抑亦近代之美也。

translations.literal: Although comprehensive Confucians' flourishing achievements did not reach the ministers of Wei and Jin, yet the wind shifted and customs changed—this too was a beauty of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Though the great Confucian achievements did not match those of Wei and Jin times, the transformation of customs was nonetheless a glory of the recent age.

sentences.zh: 自正朔不一，將三百年，師訓紛綸，無所取正。

translations.literal: From when the calendar and reign titles were not unified, for nearly three hundred years, masters' instructions were tangled and confused, with nothing to take as correct.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly three hundred years, with no unified calendar or reign title, scholarly traditions were tangled and none could be taken as authoritative.

sentences.zh: 隋文膺期纂曆，平一寰宇，頓天鋼以掩之，賁旌帛以禮之，設好爵以縻之，於是四海九州，強學待問之士，靡不畢集焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui received the term and succeeded to the calendar, leveled and unified the whole realm; he suddenly lowered the heavenly net to cover them, adorned with banners and silk to treat them with ceremony, and set fine ranks to tether them—thereupon within the four seas and nine provinces, men of forceful learning awaiting inquiry, none failed to gather completely.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui received the Mandate, unified the realm, drew the net of heaven over all, honored scholars with banners and silk, and bound them with fine offices—whereupon eager students from every corner of the empire gathered without exception.

sentences.zh: 天子乃整萬乘，率百僚，遵問道之儀，觀釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven then arrayed his ten-thousand chariots, led the hundred officials, followed the ceremony of inquiring about the Way, and observed the libation ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven then arrayed his chariots, led the hundred officials, performed the ceremony of inquiring about the Way, and observed the libation rites.

sentences.zh: 博士罄縣河之辯，侍中竭重席之奧。

translations.literal: The doctors exhausted the debate of Xuanhe County; the attendants within exhausted the profundities of piled mats.
translations.idiomatic: The doctoral lecturers exhausted their eloquence like Xuanhe of old, and the palace attendants expounded the deepest mysteries from their layered seats.

sentences.zh: 考正亡逸，研核異同，積滯群疑，渙然冰釋。

translations.literal: He examined and corrected what was lost and scattered, investigated and verified differences and samenesses; accumulated and stagnant doubts of the multitude dissolved like ice melting.
translations.idiomatic: Lost texts were collated, divergent readings examined, and accumulated doubts of generations melted away like ice.

sentences.zh: 於是超擢奇俊，厚賞諸儒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he specially promoted outstanding and exceptional men and richly rewarded the various Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He then promoted exceptional scholars and richly rewarded the Confucians.

sentences.zh: 京邑達乎四方，皆啟黌校。

translations.literal: The capital reached to the four directions; everywhere schools were opened.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to the four corners of the realm, schools were established.

sentences.zh: 齊魯趙魏，學者尤多。

translations.literal: In Qi, Lu, Zhao, and Wei, scholars were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Lu, Zhao, and Wei had especially large numbers of scholars.

sentences.zh: 負笈追師，不遠千里，講誦之聲，道路不絕。

translations.literal: Those who bore satchels and pursued teachers did not regard a thousand li as far; the sound of lecturing and recitation on the roads never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Students traveled a thousand li to follow teachers, and the sound of lectures never ceased along the roads.

sentences.zh: 中州之盛，自漢魏以來，一時而已。

translations.literal: The flourishing of the Central Plains—since Han and Wei, there had been only this one moment.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains had not seen such scholarly flourishing since Han and Wei times.

sentences.zh: 及帝暮年，精華稍竭，不悅儒術，專尚刑名，執政之徒，咸非篤好。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached his later years, his vital essence gradually waned; he did not delight in Confucian arts but exclusively honored penal names; those who held power were all not ardent lovers of learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor lost interest in Confucian learning and favored penal law instead; those in power no longer cared for scholarship.

sentences.zh: 暨仁壽間，遂廢天下之學，唯存國子一所，弟子七十二人。

translations.literal: By the Renshou era, schools throughout the realm were abolished; only one National University remained, with seventy-two disciples.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era all schools in the realm were closed; only the National University remained, with seventy-two students.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，復開庠序，國子、郡縣之學，盛於開皇之初。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he again opened schools; the National University and commandery and county schools flourished as at the beginning of Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang reopened the schools, and the National University and local schools flourished as they had at the start of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 徽辟儒生，遠近畢至。

translations.literal: He summoned and recruited Confucian scholars; from near and far all arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Confucian scholars, and they came from far and near.

sentences.zh: 使相與講論得失於東都之下，納言定其差次，一以聞奏焉。

translations.literal: He had them discuss gains and losses with one another below the Eastern Capital; the Director of Speech determined their ranking and reported all to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars debated their views below the Eastern Capital; the Director of Speech ranked their conclusions and reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 于時，舊儒多已凋亡，惟信都劉士元、河間劉光伯拔萃出類，學通南北，博極今古，後生鑽仰。

translations.literal: At that time the old Confucians had mostly perished; only Liu Shiyuan of Xindu and Liu Guangbo of Hejian stood out from the crowd, their learning penetrating north and south and exhaustively reaching present and past—later students drilled into and looked up to them.
translations.idiomatic: By then most of the old scholars had died; only Liu Shiyuan of Xindu and Liu Guangbo of Hejian stood out, masters of learning north and south and past and present, whom younger scholars revered.

sentences.zh: 所制諸經義疏，縉紳咸師宗之。

translations.literal: The commentaries on the classics they composed were all taken as masters by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: The commentaries on the classics they wrote were adopted as standard texts by the gentry.

sentences.zh: 既而外事四夷，戎馬不息，師徒怠散，盜賊群起。

translations.literal: Afterward he turned to external affairs with the four barbarians; war-horses never rested; teachers and students grew slack and scattered; bandits rose in groups.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to foreign campaigns; war never ceased; teachers and students dispersed; and bandits rose everywhere.

sentences.zh: 禮義不足以防君子，刑罰不足以威小人，空有建學之名，而無弘道之實。

translations.literal: Ritual and righteousness were insufficient to guard against gentlemen; punishments and penalties were insufficient to awe petty men—emptyly there was the name of establishing schools, yet no reality of spreading the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual could no longer restrain the noble, nor punishment terrify the base; schools existed in name only, with no real promotion of learning.

sentences.zh: 其風漸墜，以至滅亡。

translations.literal: Its wind gradually fell, until it reached extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Learning declined steadily until it was extinguished altogether.

sentences.zh: 方領矩步之徒，亦轉死溝壑，凡有經籍，因此湮沒於煨燼矣。

translations.literal: Those who wore square collars and measured their steps also in turn died in ditches and gullies; all classical texts thereby sank and were lost in embers and ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in their ceremonial dress perished in ditches and gullies, and countless classical texts were consumed in the flames.

sentences.zh: 遂使後進之士，不復聞《詩書》之言，皆懷攘竊之心，相與陷於不義。

translations.literal: Thus the students who came after no longer heard the words of the Odes and Documents; all harbored hearts of plunder and theft, and together they fell into unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations never heard the words of the Odes and Documents; all nursed hearts of plunder, and together they sank into unrighteousness.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「學者將殖，不學者將落。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "Those who study will flourish; those who do not study will decline."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "Those who study will flourish; those who do not study will decline."

sentences.zh: 然則盛衰是系，興亡攸在，有國有家者，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Then prosperity and decline are tethered to this; rise and fall reside herein—those who have states and families, can they not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Surely then prosperity and decline depend on learning, and rise and fall upon it—how can rulers of states and clans fail to be cautious!

sentences.zh: 漢世，鄭玄並為眾經注解，服虔、何休，各有所說。

translations.literal: In the Han age, Zheng Xuan together made commentaries on all the classics; Fu Qian and He Xiu each had their own explanations.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Zheng Xuan commented on all the classics, while Fu Qian and He Xiu each had their own schools of interpretation.

sentences.zh: 玄《易》、《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《論語》、《孝經》，虔《左氏春秋》，休《公羊傳》，大行于河北。

translations.literal: Xuan's commentaries on the Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, Fu Qian's Zuo's Spring and Autumn, and He Xiu's Gongyang Commentary all flourished greatly in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentaries on the Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, Fu Qian's Zuo Commentary, and He Xiu's Gongyang Commentary all flourished in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 王肅《易》，亦間行焉。

translations.literal: Wang Su's Changes also circulated there from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's commentary on the Changes also circulated there occasionally.

sentences.zh: 晉世，杜預注《左氏》。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, Du Yu commented on the Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times Du Yu commented on the Zuo Tradition.

sentences.zh: 預玄孫坦，坦弟驥，于宋朝並為青州刺史，傳其家業，故齊地多習之。

translations.literal: Yu's great-grandson Tan and Tan's younger brother Ji, in the Song dynasty both served as governors of Qing province and transmitted their family profession; thus the Qi region largely practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's great-grandson Tan and Tan's younger brother Ji, who in the Song both served as governors of Qing province, transmitted the family learning, so the Qi region largely followed Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 自魏末，大儒徐遵明門下講鄭玄所注《周易》。

translations.literal: From the end of Wei, the great Confucian Xu Zunming lectured on Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Changes among his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Wei period, the great scholar Xu Zunming taught Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Changes to his disciples.

sentences.zh: 遵明以傳盧景裕及清河崔瑾。

translations.literal: Zunming transmitted it to Lu Jingyu and Cui Jin of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming passed it on to Lu Jingyu and Cui Jin of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 景裕傳權會、郭茂。

translations.literal: Jingyu transmitted it to Quan Hui and Guo Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu passed it to Quan Hui and Guo Mao.

sentences.zh: 權會早入鄴都，郭茂恆在門下教授，其後能言《易》者，多出郭茂之門。

translations.literal: Hui early entered the capital at Ye; Guo Mao constantly taught among the disciples; afterward those who could discourse on the Changes mostly came from Guo Mao's school.
translations.idiomatic: Hui entered Ye early; Guo Mao remained teaching at the gate; afterward most who could expound the Changes came from Guo Mao's school.

sentences.zh: 河南及青齊之間，儒生多講王輔嗣所注，師訓蓋寡。

translations.literal: Between Henan and Qing and Qi, Confucian scholars mostly lectured on Wang Fuzhi's commentary; masters' instructions were scant.
translations.idiomatic: Between Henan and Qing and Qi, scholars mostly taught Wang Bi's commentary, with few traditional lineages.

sentences.zh: 齊時，儒士罕傳《尚書》之業，徐遵明兼通之。

translations.literal: In Qi times, Confucian scholars rarely transmitted the profession of the Documents; Xu Zunming mastered it as well.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi, few scholars transmitted the Book of Documents; Xu Zunming was among those who did.

sentences.zh: 遵明受業于屯留王聰，傳授浮陽李周仁及勃海張文敬、李鉉、河間權會，並鄭康成所注，非古文也。

translations.literal: Zunming received instruction from Wang Cong of Tunliu and transmitted to Li Zhouren of Fuyang, Zhang Wenjing, Li Xuan, and Quan Hui of Bohai and Hejian—all Zheng Xuan's commentary, not the ancient text.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming studied under Wang Cong of Tunliu and taught Li Zhouren of Fuyang, Zhang Wenjing, Li Xuan, and Quan Hui—all using Zheng Xuan's commentary, not the ancient text version.

sentences.zh: 下里諸生，略不見孔氏注解。

translations.literal: Rustic students below barely saw Confucius's commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Village students below rarely encountered Confucius's own commentaries.

sentences.zh: 武平末，劉光伯、劉士元始得費甝《義疏》，乃留意焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping, Liu Guangbo and Liu Shiyuan first obtained Fei Kan's Meaning and Commentary and then gave it attention.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping, Liu Guangbo and Liu Shiyuan first obtained Fei Kan's commentary and took it up.

sentences.zh: 其《詩》、《禮》、《春秋》，尤為當時所尚，諸生多兼通之。

translations.literal: The Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn were especially honored at that time; most students mastered several of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn were especially prized; most students mastered several of these.

sentences.zh: 《三禮》並出遵明之門。

translations.literal: The Three Rites all came from Zunming's gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rites all issued from Zunming's school.

sentences.zh: 徐傳業于李鉉、祖俊、田元鳳、馮傳、紀顯敬、呂黃龍、夏懷敬。

translations.literal: Xu transmitted the profession to Li Xuan, Zu Jun, Tian Yuanfeng, Feng Chuan, Ji Xianjing, Lü Huanglong, and Xia Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu passed the tradition to Li Xuan, Zu Jun, Tian Yuanfeng, Feng Chuan, Ji Xianjing, Lü Huanglong, and Xia Huaijing.

sentences.zh: 李鉉又傳授刁柔、張買奴、鮑季詳、邢峙、劉晝、熊安生。

translations.literal: Li Xuan again transmitted to Diao Rou, Zhang Mainu, Bao Jixiang, Xing Zhi, Liu Zhou, and Xiong Ansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan in turn taught Diao Rou, Zhang Mainu, Bao Jixiang, Xing Zhi, Liu Zhou, and Xiong Ansheng.

sentences.zh: 安生又傳孫靈暉、郭仲堅、丁恃德。

translations.literal: Ansheng again transmitted to Sun Linghui, Guo Zhongjian, and Ding Side.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng passed it to Sun Linghui, Guo Zhongjian, and Ding Side.

sentences.zh: 其後生能通《禮經》者，多是安生門人。

translations.literal: Afterward students who could penetrate the Book of Rites were mostly Ansheng's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars who mastered the Book of Rites were mostly disciples of Ansheng.

sentences.zh: 諸生盡通《小戴禮》。

translations.literal: All students thoroughly mastered the Elder Dai's Rites.
translations.idiomatic: All students thoroughly mastered the Elder Dai's Rites.

sentences.zh: 于《周儀禮》兼通者，十二三焉。

translations.literal: Of those who also mastered the Zhou Ceremonial Rites, there were one or two out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Only one or two in ten also mastered the Zhou Ceremonial Rites.

sentences.zh: 通《毛詩》者，多出於魏朝劉獻之。

translations.literal: Those who mastered the Mao Odes mostly came from Liu Xianzhi of the Wei court.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of the Mao Odes mostly descended from Liu Xianzhi of Wei.

sentences.zh: 獻之傳李周仁。

translations.literal: Xianzhi transmitted to Li Zhouren.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi passed it to Li Zhouren.

sentences.zh: 周仁傳董令度、程歸則。

translations.literal: Zhouren transmitted to Dong Lingdu and Cheng Guize.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouren taught Dong Lingdu and Cheng Guize.

sentences.zh: 歸則傳劉敬和、張思伯、劉軌思。

translations.literal: Guize transmitted to Liu Jinghe, Zhang Sibo, and Liu Guisi.
translations.idiomatic: Guize passed it to Liu Jinghe, Zhang Sibo, and Liu Guisi.

sentences.zh: 其後能言《詩》者，多出二劉之門。

translations.literal: Afterward those who could discourse on the Odes mostly came from the two Liu's gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later expounders of the Odes mostly came from the two Liu schools.

sentences.zh: 河北諸儒能通《春秋》者，並服子慎所注，亦出徐生之門。

translations.literal: Confucians north of the river who could penetrate the Spring and Autumn all used Fu Zishen's commentary, which also came from Xu's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Northern scholars who mastered the Spring and Autumn all used Fu Qian's commentary, also from Xu's line.

sentences.zh: 張買奴、馬敬德、邢峙、張思伯、張奉禮、張彫、劉晝、鮑長宣、王元則並得服氏之精微。

translations.literal: Zhang Mainu, Ma Jingde, Xing Zhi, Zhang Sibo, Zhang Fengli, Zhang Diao, Liu Zhou, Bao Changxuan, and Wang Yuanze all obtained the subtlety of the Fu school.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mainu, Ma Jingde, Xing Zhi, Zhang Sibo, Zhang Fengli, Zhang Diao, Liu Zhou, Bao Changxuan, and Wang Yuanze all mastered Fu Qian's subtle teachings.

sentences.zh: 又有衛覬、陳達、潘叔虔，雖不傳徐氏之門，亦為通解。

translations.literal: There were also Wei Ji, Chen Da, and Pan Shuqian; although they did not transmit from Xu's gate, they too had penetrating understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji, Chen Da, and Pan Shuqian, though outside Xu's line, also achieved thorough understanding.

sentences.zh: 又有姚文安、秦道靜，初亦學服氏，後兼更講杜元凱所注。

translations.literal: There were also Yao Wen'an and Qin Daojing; at first they too studied the Fu school, but later additionally lectured on Du Yuankai's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wen'an and Qin Daojing first studied Fu Qian, then also taught Du Yu's commentary.

sentences.zh: 其河外儒生，俱伏膺杜氏。

translations.literal: Confucian students beyond the river all bowed their chests to the Du school.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars south of the Yellow River all followed the Du school.

sentences.zh: 其《公羊》、《谷梁》二傳，儒者多不厝懷。

translations.literal: The Gongyang and Guliang commentaries—most Confucians did not place them in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang and Guliang commentaries drew little interest from most scholars.

sentences.zh: 《論語》、《孝經》，諸學徒莫不通講。

translations.literal: The Analects and Classic of Filial Piety—all students lectured on them without exception.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects and Classic of Filial Piety were lectured on by every student without exception.

sentences.zh: 諸儒如權會、李欽、刁柔、熊安生、劉軌思、馬敬德之徒，多自出義疏。

translations.literal: Confucians such as Quan Hui, Li Qin, Diao Rou, Xiong Ansheng, Liu Guisi, and Ma Jingde mostly produced their own commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars such as Quan Hui, Li Qin, Diao Rou, Xiong Ansheng, Liu Guisi, and Ma Jingde mostly wrote their own commentaries.

sentences.zh: 雖曰專門，亦皆相祖習也。

translations.literal: Although they were called specialists, they all likewise inherited and practiced from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Though called specialists, they all inherited from one another's traditions.

sentences.zh: 大抵南北所為章句，好尚互有不同。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, the chapter-and-verse commentaries made north and south had preferences that mutually differed.
translations.idiomatic: In general, the commentarial traditions of north and south differed in their preferences.

sentences.zh: 江左，《周易》則王輔嗣，《尚書》則孔安國，《左傅》則杜元凱。

translations.literal: In the lands south of the Yangtze, for the Book of Changes it was Wang Fuzhi; for the Documents it was Kong Anguo; for the Zuo Tradition it was Du Yuankai.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze, the Changes followed Wang Bi, the Documents Kong Anguo, and the Zuo Tradition Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 河洛，《左傳》則服子慎，《尚書》、《周易》則鄭康成。

translations.literal: In the He and Luo regions, for the Zuo Tradition it was Fu Zishen; for the Documents and Changes it was Zheng Kangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the He and Luo regions, the Zuo Tradition followed Fu Qian, the Documents and Changes Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 《詩》則並主于毛公，《禮》則同遵于鄭氏。

translations.literal: For the Odes both upheld the Mao school; for the Rites both followed the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: Both regions upheld the Mao Odes and followed the Zheng Rites.

sentences.zh: 南人約簡，得其英華；

translations.literal: Southerners were concise and obtained the essence and flower;
translations.idiomatic: Southern learning was concise and grasped the essentials;

sentences.zh: 北學深蕪，窮其枝葉。

translations.literal: Northern learning was deep and overgrown, exhausting branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Northern learning was exhaustive but overgrown, pursuing every branch and leaf.

sentences.zh: 考其終始，要其會歸，其立身成名，殊方同致矣。

translations.literal: Examining their beginning and end, grasping their meeting and return—in establishing themselves and achieving fame, different regions attained the same goal.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing their courses to the end, both paths led to the same achievement of fame and standing.

sentences.zh: 自魏梁越已下，傳授講議者甚眾，今各依時代而次，以備《儒林》云爾。

translations.literal: From Liang Yue of Wei downward, those who transmitted and lectured were very numerous; now each is arranged according to era in sequence, to complete the Confucian Forest.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang Yue of Wei onward, transmitters and lecturers were very numerous; they are here arranged by era to complete this account of the Confucian Forest.

sentences.zh: 梁越，字玄覽，新興人也。

translations.literal: Liang Yue, styled Xuanlan, was a man of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yue, courtesy name Xuanlan, was from Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 博通經傳，性純和。

translations.literal: He thoroughly penetrated the classics and transmissions and was pure and harmonious by nature.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and commentaries and was gentle by nature.

sentences.zh: 魏初，為《禮經》博士。

translations.literal: In early Wei he served as doctor of the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wei he served as doctor of the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 道武以其謹厚，遷上大夫，令授諸皇子經書。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu, because of his prudence and solidity, promoted him to Grand Master and ordered him to teach the imperial princes the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu, valuing his prudence and integrity, promoted him to Grand Master and had him instruct the princes in the classics.

sentences.zh: 明元初，以師傅恩，賜爵祝阿侯，出為雁門太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan, because of his merit as a teacher, he was granted the title Marquis of Zhu'e and sent out as governor of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Mingyuan, in recognition of his service as tutor, he was made Marquis of Zhu'e and appointed governor of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 獲白雀以獻，拜光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He obtained a white sparrow and presented it; he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a white sparrow as tribute, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died.

sentences.zh: 盧醜，昌黎徒何人也。

translations.literal: Lu Chou, a man of Tuhe in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chou was from Tuhe in Changli.

sentences.zh: 襄城王魯元之族也。

translations.literal: He was of the clan of Prince Lu Yuan of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He belonged to the clan of Prince Lu Yuan of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 太武監國，醜以博學入授經。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu supervised the state, Chou entered to teach the classics because of his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu was regent, Chou was brought in to teach the classics for his erudition.

sentences.zh: 後以師傅舊恩，賜爵濟陰公。

translations.literal: Later, because of his old merit as a teacher, he was granted the title Duke of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in recognition of his service as tutor, he was made Duke of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 位尚書，加散騎常侍，卒于河內太守。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Minister, was additionally appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and died while serving as governor of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister, was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and died as governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 張偉，字仲業，太原中都人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, styled Zhongye, was a man of Zhongdu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, courtesy name Zhongye, was from Zhongdu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 學通諸經。

translations.literal: His learning penetrated all the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered all the classics.

sentences.zh: 鄉里受業者，常數百人。

translations.literal: Those who received instruction from him in his village regularly numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred students regularly studied under him in his home district.

sentences.zh: 儒謹泛納。

translations.literal: He was broadly tolerant in accepting students.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted students broadly and tolerantly.

sentences.zh: 雖有頑固，問至數十，偉告喻殷勤，曾無慍色。

translations.literal: Although some were stubborn, asking dozens of questions, Wei instructed and admonished them earnestly and never showed anger.
translations.idiomatic: Even the most stubborn, who asked the same question dozens of times, found him patient and never angry.

sentences.zh: 常依附經典，教以孝悌，門人感其仁化，事之如父。

translations.literal: He constantly relied on the classics to teach filial piety and brotherly duty; his disciples were moved by his humane transformation and served him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly drew on the classics to teach filial piety and brotherly duty; his students, moved by his humane influence, served him as a father.

sentences.zh: 性清雅，非法不言。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and elegant; he spoke nothing contrary to law.
translations.idiomatic: He was refined in character and spoke only what was proper.

sentences.zh: 太武時，與高允等俱被辟命，授中書博士，累遷為中書侍郎，本國大中正。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taiwu, together with Gao Yun and others he was summoned and appointed Secretariat Doctor, and was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he was summoned with Gao Yun and others, appointed Secretariat Doctor, and rose to Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Rectifier of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 使酒泉慰勞沮渠無諱，又使宋，賜爵成皋子。

translations.literal: He was sent to Jiuquan to comfort Juqu Wuhui, and also sent to Song; he was granted the title Viscount of Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Jiuquan to console Juqu Wuhui and also as envoy to Song, and was granted the title Viscount of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 出為營州刺史，進爵建安公。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Yingzhou and was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Yingzhou and advanced to Duke of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈并州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made governor of Bingzhou with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made governor of Bingzhou with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 梁祚，北地泥陽人也。

translations.literal: Liang Zuo, a man of Niyang in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zuo was from Niyang in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 父邵，皇始二年歸魏，位濟陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Shao submitted to Wei in the second year of Huangshi and reached the post of governor of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao submitted to Wei in the second year of Huangshi and became governor of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 至祚，居趙郡。

translations.literal: By the time of Zuo, the family resided in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By Zuo's time the family had settled in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祚篤志好學，曆習經典，尤善《公羊春秋》、鄭氏《易》，常以教授。

translations.literal: Zuo was ardent in will and loved learning; he went through the classics in succession and was especially skilled in the Gongyang Spring and Autumn and Zheng's Changes, which he constantly used in teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was devoted to learning, studied the classics thoroughly, and was especially skilled in the Gongyang Spring and Autumn and Zheng Xuan's Changes, which he taught constantly.

sentences.zh: 有儒者風，而無當世之才。

translations.literal: He had the air of a Confucian but lacked talent for his own age.
translations.idiomatic: He had the bearing of a scholar but lacked talent for practical affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 與幽州別駕平恆有舊，恆時請與論經史。

translations.literal: He was old friends with the Commandery Assistant of Youzhou, Ping Heng, who often invited him to discuss the classics and history.
translations.idiomatic: He was old friends with Ping Heng, Commandery Assistant of Youzhou, who often invited him to discuss classics and history.

sentences.zh: 辟秘書中散，稍遷秘書令，為李䐶所排擯，退為中書博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Regular Attendant, was gradually promoted to Secretariat Director, was squeezed out by Li Chong, and was demoted to Secretariat Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Secretariat Regular Attendant, rose to Secretariat Director, was forced out by Li Chong, and was demoted to Secretariat Doctor.

sentences.zh: 後出為統萬鎮司馬，徵為散令。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Military Administrator of Tongwan and was recalled as Regular of the Scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Military Administrator of Tongwan and was recalled as Regular of the Scattered.

sentences.zh: 撰並陳壽《三國志》，名曰《國統》。

translations.literal: He compiled Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms and titled it National Succession.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms under the title National Succession.

sentences.zh: 又作《代都賦》，頗行於世。

translations.literal: He also wrote the Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai, which circulated widely in its time.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai, which enjoyed wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 清貧守素，不交勢貴，卒。

translations.literal: Poor and upright, keeping to simplicity, he did not associate with the powerful and noble, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in poverty and integrity, kept aloof from the powerful, and died.

sentences.zh: 子元吉，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Yuanji had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanji inherited his father's character.

sentences.zh: 平恆，字繼叔，燕郡薊人也。

translations.literal: Ping Heng, styled Jishu, was a man of Ji in Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Heng, courtesy name Jishu, was from Ji in Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖視、父儒，並仕慕容為通宦。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi and father Ru both served Murong as general officials.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi and father Ru both served the Murong as general officials.

sentences.zh: 恆耽勤讀誦，多通博聞。

translations.literal: Heng was addicted to diligent reading and recitation and was broadly learned and well-informed.
translations.idiomatic: Heng devoted himself to reading and recitation and was widely learned.

sentences.zh: 自周以降，暨于魏世，帝王傳代之由，貴臣升降之緒，皆撰品第，商略是非，號曰《略注》，合百餘篇。

translations.literal: From Zhou downward through the Wei age, the reasons for imperial succession and the threads of noble ministers' rise and fall—he composed rankings for all, weighed right and wrong, and titled it Brief Notes, over a hundred chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou through Wei he compiled rankings of dynastic succession and ministerial careers, weighing right and wrong in a work titled Brief Notes of over a hundred chapters.

sentences.zh: 安貧樂道，不以屢空改操。

translations.literal: Content with poverty, he delighted in the Way and did not alter his conduct because of repeated emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was content in poverty and devoted to the Way, never changing his principles despite his empty purse.

sentences.zh: 徵為中書博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Secretariat Doctor.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為幽州別駕。

translations.literal: After a long time, he went out as Commandery Assistant of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Commandery Assistant of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 廉貞寡欲，不營資產，衣食至常不足，妻子不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Upright and few in desires, he did not manage assets; food and clothing were often insufficient, and wife and children could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and frugal, kept no property, and often lacked food and clothing; his wife and children knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 後遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Secretariat Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Secretariat Assistant.

sentences.zh: 時高允為監，河間邢祐、北平陽嘏、河東裴宗、廣平程駿、金城趙元順等為著作郎。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Yun was Director; Xing You of Hejian, Yang Gu of Beiping, Pei Zong of Hedong, Cheng Jun of Guangping, Zhao Yuanshun of Jincheng, and others served as Composition Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Yun was Director; Xing You, Yang Gu, Pei Zong, Cheng Jun, Zhao Yuanshun, and others served as Composition Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 允每稱博通經籍，無過恆也。

translations.literal: Yun always praised that in penetrating the classics and records, none surpassed Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun always said that in mastery of the classics, none surpassed Heng.

sentences.zh: 恆三子，並不率父業，好酒自棄。

translations.literal: Heng's three sons all failed to follow their father's profession; they loved wine and abandoned themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's three sons all failed to follow their father's path; they took to drink and ruined themselves.

sentences.zh: 恆常忿其世衰，植杖巡舍，側崗而哭。

translations.literal: Heng often resented the decline of his age; leaning on his staff he walked around his house and wept beside the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Heng often grieved the decline of his age; leaning on his staff he paced his compound and wept beside the family mound.

sentences.zh: 不為營事婚宦，任意官娶，曰：「此輩會是衰頓，何煩勞我！」

translations.literal: He did not arrange marriages for them but let them marry as officials pleased, saying: "These fellows are sure to be in decline—why should I trouble myself!"
translations.idiomatic: He arranged no marriages for them but let them wed as they pleased, saying, "These sons are bound for ruin—why should I trouble myself!"

sentences.zh: 故仕娉濁碎，不得及其門流。

translations.literal: Therefore officials they married were coarse and base, unable to match his family's standing.
translations.idiomatic: The officials they married were coarse and base, unworthy of his family's standing.

sentences.zh: 別構精廬，並置經籍於中，一奴自給，妻子莫得而往，酒食亦不與同。

translations.literal: He separately built a refined lodge, placed the classics within it, and had one slave attend him; wife and children might not go there, nor share food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: He built a separate study lodge stocked with classics, attended by a single servant; his wife and children were barred from entering or sharing his meals.

sentences.zh: 時有珍美，呼時老東安公刁雍等共飲啖之，家人無得嘗焉。

translations.literal: When there were delicacies, he called the venerable Duke of Dong'an, Diao Yong, and others to eat and drink with him; the family might not taste them.
translations.idiomatic: When delicacies arrived, he summoned the venerable Diao Yong and other elders to share them; his family tasted none.

sentences.zh: 太和十年，以恆為秘書令，而固請為郡，未受而卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taihe, Heng was made Secretariat Director, but he firmly requested a commandery post; before he received it he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Taihe he was appointed Secretariat Director but firmly requested a provincial post; he died before taking it up.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州刺史、都昌侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made governor of Youzhou, Marquis of Duchang, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Youzhou and Marquis of Duchang, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 陳奇，字脩奇，河北人也。

translations.literal: Chen Qi, styled Xiuqi, was a man of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qi, courtesy name Xiuqi, was from Hebei.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，而奉母至孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 齠祇聰識，有夙成之美。

translations.literal: From infancy he was intelligent and perceptive, with the beauty of early maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was bright and precocious.

sentences.zh: 愛玩經典，常非馬融、鄭玄解經失旨。

translations.literal: He loved and delighted in the classics and often criticized Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan for missing the point in interpreting the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics and often criticized Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan for misinterpreting them.

sentences.zh: 志在著述《五經》。

translations.literal: His ambition was to compose commentaries on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He aspired to write commentaries on the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 始注《孝經》、《論語》，頗傳於世，為縉紳所稱。

translations.literal: He first commented on the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects, which circulated widely and were praised by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects circulated widely and won praise from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 與河間邢祐同召赴京。

translations.literal: Together with Xing You of Hejian he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital together with Xing You of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 時秘書省游雅素聞其名，始頗好之，引入秘省，欲授以史職。

translations.literal: At that time You Ya of the Secretariat had long heard his name, at first favored him greatly, brought him into the Secretariat, and wished to give him a historiographical post.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya of the Secretariat had long heard of him, favored him at first, brought him into the Secretariat, and wished to assign him historiographical duties.

sentences.zh: 後與奇論典誥，至《易訟卦》「天與水違行」，雅曰：「自蔥嶺以西，水皆西流，推此而言，自蔥嶺西，豈東向望天哉？」

translations.literal: Later he debated canonical texts with Qi; when they reached the Song hexagram of the Changes—"Heaven and water go contrary"—Ya said: "West of the Cong Mountains all waters flow west; pushing from this, west of the Cong Mountains how could one look east toward heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Later debating the classics with Qi, they reached the Song hexagram—"Heaven and water go contrary"—and Ya said: "West of the Cong Mountains all rivers flow west; how then west of the Cong Mountains could one look east toward heaven?

sentences.zh: 雅性護短，因以為嫌。

translations.literal: Ya's nature was to protect his shortcomings; because of this he bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was touchy about his errors and took offense.

sentences.zh: 嘗眾辱奇，或爾汝之，或指為小人。

translations.literal: He once humiliated Qi before a crowd, sometimes addressing him familiarly, sometimes calling him a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: He once publicly humiliated Qi, addressing him familiarly or calling him a petty man.

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「公身為君子，奇身且小人。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "Your person is that of a gentleman; my person is but a petty man."
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied: "You are a gentleman; I am but a petty man.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「君言身且小人，君祖父是何人也？」

translations.literal: Ya said: "You say your person is a petty man—what men were your grandfather and father?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya said: "You call yourself a petty man—who were your grandfather and father?

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「祖，燕東部侯厘。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "My grandfather was Marquis Li of the Eastern Division of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "My grandfather was Marquis Li of the Eastern Division of Yan.

sentences.zh: 雅質奇曰：「侯厘何官也？」

translations.literal: Ya questioned Qi: "What office was Marquis Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya demanded: "What office was Marquis Li?

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「昔有雲師、火正、鳥師之名，以斯而言，世革則官異，時易則禮變。

translations.literal: Qi said: "In antiquity there were the titles Cloud Master, Fire Rectifier, and Bird Master; from this it follows that when the age changes, offices differ; when times change, ritual transforms.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "In antiquity there were Cloud Master, Fire Rectifier, and Bird Master—when ages change, offices change; when times change, ritual changes.

sentences.zh: 公為皇魏東宮內侍長，竟何職也？」

translations.literal: You serve as Eastern Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary of Great Wei—what office is that in the end?
translations.idiomatic: You are Eastern Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary of Great Wei—what office is that?

sentences.zh: 先是，敕以奇付雅，令銓補秘書。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had assigned Qi to Ya to rank and supplement the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had earlier assigned Qi to Ya for Secretariat placement.

sentences.zh: 雅既惡之，遂不復敘用焉。

translations.literal: Ya already hated him and therefore never again recorded him for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ya, already hostile, never recommended him for appointment.

sentences.zh: 奇冗散數年，高允每嘉其遠致，稱奇通識，非凡學所及。

translations.literal: Qi was idle and scattered for several years; Gao Yun always praised his far-reaching character and said Qi's penetrating knowledge was not reached by ordinary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Qi remained idle for years; Gao Yun always praised his breadth of vision and said his learning surpassed the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 允微勸雅曰：「君朝望具瞻，何為與野儒辯簡牘章句！」

translations.literal: Yun subtly urged Ya: "Your court prestige is universally gazed upon—why debate bamboo slips and chapter-and-verse with a rustic Confucian!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun gently urged Ya: "The court looks to you—why debate chapter and verse with a rustic scholar!

sentences.zh: 雅謂允有私於奇，曰：「君寧黨小人也？」

translations.literal: Ya thought Yun was partial to Qi and said: "Would you favor a petty man?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya thought Yun favored Qi and said: "Are you siding with a petty man?

sentences.zh: 乃取奇注《論語》、《孝經》，燒於庭內。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Qi's commentaries on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety and burned them in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Qi's commentaries on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety and burned them in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「公貴人，不乏樵薪，何乃燃奇《論語》！」

translations.literal: Qi said: "Your Excellency is a noble man and lacks no firewood—why burn Qi's Analects!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "Your Excellency lacks no firewood—why burn my Analects!

sentences.zh: 雅愈怒，因告京師後生，不聽傳授。

translations.literal: Ya grew angrier and therefore told the capital's young scholars not to transmit his teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Ya grew angrier still and forbade capital students to study under him.

sentences.zh: 而奇無降志，亦評雅之失。

translations.literal: Yet Qi had no lowering of will and also criticized Ya's errors.
translations.idiomatic: Qi did not yield and continued to criticize Ya's faults.

sentences.zh: 雅制昭皇太后碑文，論後名字之美，比諭前魏之甄後。

translations.literal: Ya composed the stele inscription for Empress Dowager Zhao, discussing the beauty of the empress's name and comparing her to Empress Zhen of former Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ya wrote the stele for Empress Dowager Zhao, praising her name and comparing her to Empress Zhen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 奇刺發其非，遂聞於上。

translations.literal: Qi exposed the impropriety, and it reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Qi exposed the impropriety, and the matter reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔下司徒檢對，雅有屈焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Minister of Education to examine and compare; Ya was found at fault.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Minister of Education to investigate; Ya was found at fault.

sentences.zh: 有人為謗書，多怨時之言，頗稱奇不得志。

translations.literal: Someone wrote a slanderous book full of complaints against the times, much praising Qi's lack of success.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote a slanderous tract full of complaints, much of it praising Qi's frustrated career.

sentences.zh: 雅乃諷在事雲，此書言奇不遂，當是奇假人為之。

translations.literal: Ya then insinuated to those in office that since the book said Qi did not succeed, Qi must have had someone else write it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ya insinuated to officials that since the book lamented Qi's failure, Qi must have commissioned it.

sentences.zh: 如依律文，造謗書者，皆及孥戮。

translations.literal: According to the penal code, those who compose slanderous books are punished extending to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Under the penal code, authors of slanderous books faced punishment extending to their families.

sentences.zh: 遂抵奇罪。

translations.literal: Qi's crime was thus imputed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was charged on this basis.

sentences.zh: 時司徒、平原王陸麗知奇見枉，惜其才學，故得遷延經年，冀得寬宥。

translations.literal: At that time the Minister of Education, Prince Pingyuan Lu Li, knew Qi was wronged and valued his talent; therefore the case was delayed for years in hope of pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Prince Pingyuan Lu Li knew Qi was wronged and valued his talent, so the case dragged on for years hoping for pardon.

sentences.zh: 獄成，竟致大戮，遂及其家。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, he was put to great execution after all, and his family was implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When the case concluded, he was executed and his family implicated.

sentences.zh: 奇于《易》尤長，在獄嘗自筮。

translations.literal: Qi was especially skilled in the Changes; in prison he once divined for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was especially skilled in the Changes; in prison he divined for himself.

sentences.zh: 卦未及成，乃攬破而歎曰：「吾不度來年冬季。」

translations.literal: Before the hexagram was completed he pulled it apart and sighed: "I shall not pass the winter of next year."
translations.idiomatic: Before the hexagram was complete he tore it apart and sighed: "I shall not survive next winter.

sentences.zh: 及奇受害，如其所占。

translations.literal: When Qi suffered execution, it was as he had divined.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was executed, it happened as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 奇初被召，夜夢星墜壓腳。

translations.literal: When Qi was first summoned, he dreamed at night that a star fell and pressed his foot.
translations.idiomatic: When first summoned, he dreamed a star fell on his foot.

sentences.zh: 明而告人曰：「星則好風，星則好雨，夢星壓腳，必無善征。

translations.literal: In the morning he told others: "Stars mean fine wind; stars mean fine rain—a dream of a star pressing the foot surely has no good omen.
