translations.idiomatic: In the morning he said: "Stars mean wind and rain—a star on the foot is surely ill omen.

sentences.zh: 但時命峻切，不敢不赴耳。」

translations.literal: But the command of the age was stern and urgent; I dared not fail to go."
translations.idiomatic: But the summons was urgent; I dared not refuse."

sentences.zh: 奇外生常矯之，仕歷郡守。

translations.literal: Qi's sister's son Chang Jiao transmitted his work and served in succession as commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Chang Jiao transmitted his learning and became commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 奇所注《論語》矯之傳掌，未能行於世。

translations.literal: The Analects Qi commented on was transmitted in Jiao's keeping but could not circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's commentary on the Analects passed through Jiao but did not circulate widely.

sentences.zh: 其義多異鄭玄，往往與司徒崔浩同。

translations.literal: Its meanings often differed from Zheng Xuan and frequently agreed with Minister Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Its interpretations often differed from Zheng Xuan and often agreed with Minister Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 劉獻之，博陵饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xianzhi was a man of Raoyang in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xianzhi was from Raoyang in Boling.

sentences.zh: 少而孤貧，雅好《詩》《傳》。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he elegantly loved the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he loved the Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 曾受業于勃海程玄，後遂博觀眾籍。

translations.literal: He once received instruction from Cheng Xuan of Bohai and afterward broadly viewed numerous records.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Cheng Xuan of Bohai and later read widely.

sentences.zh: 見名法之言，掩卷而笑曰：「若使楊、墨之流，不為此書，千載誰知其小也？」

translations.literal: Seeing writings on name and law, he closed the scroll and laughed: "If Yang and Mo had not written this book, who after a thousand years would know their pettiness?"
translations.idiomatic: Reading legalist texts, he closed the scroll and laughed: "Without such books, who would remember Yang and Mo's pettiness a thousand years hence?

sentences.zh: 曾謂其所親曰：「觀屈原《離騷》之作，自是狂人，死其宜矣。

translations.literal: He once told those close to him: "Reading Qu Yuan's Encounter with Sorrow—by nature he was a madman; death suited him.
translations.idiomatic: He told intimates: "Qu Yuan's Encounter with Sorrow shows a born madman—death suited him.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰'無可無不可'，實獲我心。」

translations.literal: Confucius said 'nothing is necessary, nothing is forbidden'—that truly obtained my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said 'nothing is necessary, nothing is forbidden'—that is my view.

sentences.zh: 時人有從獻之學者，獻之輒謂之曰：「人之立身，雖百行殊塗，准之四科，要以德行為首。

translations.literal: When people came to study with Xianzhi, he always told them: "In establishing oneself, though the hundred practices have different paths, measured against the four categories, conduct and virtue must come first.
translations.idiomatic: To students he said: "Though paths differ, conduct and virtue must come first.

sentences.zh: 子若能入孝出悌，忠信仁讓，不待出戶，天下自知。

translations.literal: If you can enter with filial piety and exit with brotherly duty, loyalty, trustworthiness, benevolence, and forbearance, without leaving your door the realm will know you of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If you practice filial piety, brotherly duty, loyalty, and benevolence at home, the world will know you without your leaving it.

sentences.zh: 儻不能然，雖復下帷針股，躡屩從師，正可博聞多識，不過為土龍乞雨，眩惑將來。

translations.literal: If you cannot, though you lower the curtain and thread the needle, treading sandals to follow teachers, you may only gain broad hearing and much knowledge—no more than a clay dragon praying for rain, dazzling those to come.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, though you study tirelessly under masters, you gain only book learning—like a clay dragon praying for rain, dazzling others to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 其於立身之道，有何益乎？

translations.literal: What benefit is there for the way of establishing oneself?
translations.idiomatic: What good is that for how one lives?

sentences.zh: 孔門之徒，初亦未悟，見皋魚之歎，方乃歸而養親。

translations.literal: Confucius's disciples at first also did not understand; seeing Gao Yu's lament, only then did they return to nourish their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's disciples at first failed to understand; only Gao Yu's lament moved them to care for their parents.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 先達何自覺之晚也？」

translations.literal: How late did the former worthies awaken!"
translations.idiomatic: How late the ancients awakened to this!

sentences.zh: 由是四方學者，莫不高其行義，希造其門。

translations.literal: Because of this scholars from the four directions all esteemed his conduct and righteousness and hoped to reach his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from all directions esteemed his conduct and sought his instruction.

sentences.zh: 獻之善《春秋》、《毛詩》。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was skilled in the Spring and Autumn and Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi excelled in the Spring and Autumn and Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 每講《左氏》，盡隱公八年便止，云：「義例已了，不復須解。」

translations.literal: Each time he lectured on the Zuo Tradition he stopped at the eighth year of Duke Yin, saying: "The principles and examples are complete; no further explanation is needed."
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on the Zuo Tradition he stopped at Duke Yin's eighth year, saying: "The principles are complete; no more is needed.

sentences.zh: 由是弟子不能究竟其說。

translations.literal: Therefore his disciples could not fully master his explanations.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples therefore never mastered the full text.

sentences.zh: 後本郡逼舉孝廉，至京稱病而還。

translations.literal: Later his native commandery compelled him to be recommended as filial and incorrupt; he reached the capital, claimed illness, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: His commandery nominated him as filial and incorrupt; he reached the capital, pleaded illness, and returned.

sentences.zh: 孝文幸中山，詔徵典內校書。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen visited Zhongshan and ordered him summoned to supervise collation within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen visited Zhongshan and summoned him to supervise palace collation.

sentences.zh: 獻之喟然歎曰：「吾不如莊周散木遠矣，一之謂甚，其可再乎！」

translations.literal: Xianzhi sighed and said: "I am far inferior to Zhuang Zhou's useless timber; once was too much—how could it be twice!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi sighed: "I am no Zhuang Zhou's useless timber—once is too much, how twice!

sentences.zh: 固以疾辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 時中山張吾貴與獻之齊名，四海皆稱儒宗。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan was equally famous with Xianzhi; within the four seas all called them Confucian patriarchs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan was equally famous; all called them Confucian patriarchs.

sentences.zh: 吾貴每一講唱，門徒千數，其行業可稱者寡。

translations.literal: Each time Wugui lectured, his disciples numbered in the thousands, yet few among them had conduct that could be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui drew thousands to his lectures, yet few among them were truly worthy.

sentences.zh: 獻之著錄，數百而已，皆通經之士。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's register had only several hundred, yet all were men who had mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's register held only several hundred, all masters of the classics.

sentences.zh: 於是有識者辨其優劣。

translations.literal: Thereupon those with discernment distinguished their superiority and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Discerning observers judged their relative merit.

sentences.zh: 魏承喪亂之後，《五經》大義，雖有師說，而海內諸生，多有疑滯，咸決於獻之。

translations.literal: Wei inherited after the age of disorder; the great meaning of the Five Classics, though there were masters' explanations, had many doubts among students within the seas—all were resolved by Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's disorders, though masters explained the Five Classics, students' doubts were resolved by Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 六藝之文，雖不悉注，所標宗旨，頗異舊義。

translations.literal: Though he did not comment on all texts of the six arts, the principles he marked often differed from old meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not comment on every art, his principles often differed from tradition.

sentences.zh: 撰《三禮大義》四卷，《三傳略例》三卷，注《毛詩序義》一卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He composed Great Meaning of the Three Rites in four chapters, Brief Examples of the Three Commentaries in three chapters, and Meaning of the Mao Odes Preface in one chapter, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Great Meaning of the Three Rites, Brief Examples of the Three Commentaries, and Meaning of the Mao Odes Preface, all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 並立《章句疏》二卷。

translations.literal: He also established Chapter-and-Verse Commentary in two chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Chapter-and-Verse Commentary in two chapters.

sentences.zh: 注《涅槃經》，未就而卒。

translations.literal: He commented on the Nirvana Sutra but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: He began a commentary on the Nirvana Sutra but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 四子：放古、爰古、參古、脩古。

translations.literal: Four sons: Fanggu, Aigu, Cangu, and Xiugu.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Fanggu, Aigu, Cangu, and Xiugu.

sentences.zh: 張吾貴，字吳子，中山人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wugui, styled Wuzi, was a man of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wugui, courtesy name Wuzi, was from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧口辯，身長八尺，容貌奇偉。

translations.literal: Young, clever in speech and debate, eight chi in height, with a strange and grand appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Clever in debate as a youth, eight chi tall, with a striking appearance.

sentences.zh: 年十八，本郡舉為太學博士。

translations.literal: At eighteen his commandery recommended him as Imperial Academy doctor.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen his commandery recommended him as Imperial Academy doctor.

sentences.zh: 吾貴先未多學，乃從酈詮受《禮》，牛天祐受《易》。

translations.literal: Wugui had not studied much at first; he received the Rites from Li Quan and the Changes from Niu Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui had little prior study; he received the Rites from Li Quan and the Changes from Niu Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 詮、祐粗為開發而已，吾貴覽讀一遍，便即別構戶牖，世人競歸之。

translations.literal: Quan and Tianyou only roughly opened the way for him; Wugui read through once and at once constructed his own doors and windows—men of the age all flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: His teachers only opened the way; Wugui read once and formed his own school—scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 曾在夏學，聚徒千數，而不講《傳》。

translations.literal: He once taught at the summer school, gathering over a thousand disciples, yet did not lecture on the Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: At summer school he gathered over a thousand students but did not lecture on the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 生徒竊云：「張生之于《左氏》，似不能說。」

translations.literal: Disciples whispered: "Master Zhang regarding the Zuo seems unable to expound it."
translations.idiomatic: Students whispered: "Master Zhang seems unable to expound the Zuo.

sentences.zh: 吾貴聞之，謂曰：「我今夏講暫罷，後當說《傳》。

translations.literal: Wugui heard and told them: "My summer lectures pause for now; later I shall expound the Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui heard and said: "Summer lectures pause for now; I shall expound the Commentary later.

sentences.zh: 君等來日，皆當持本。」

translations.literal: You will all bring your texts tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: You will all bring your texts tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 生徒怪之而已。

translations.literal: The disciples merely found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: The students only found it odd.

sentences.zh: 吾貴詣劉蘭，蘭遂為講《傳》。

translations.literal: Wugui visited Liu Lan, and Lan thereupon lectured on the Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui went to Liu Lan, who then lectured on the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 三旬之中，吾貴兼讀杜、服，隱括兩家，異同悉舉。

translations.literal: Within thirty days Wugui concurrently read Du and Fu, summarizing both schools and citing all their differences and agreements.
translations.idiomatic: In thirty days Wugui read both Du Yu and Fu Qian, compared both schools, and noted every point of agreement and difference.

sentences.zh: 諸生後集，便為講之，義例無窮，皆多新異，蘭仍伏聽。

translations.literal: When the students later assembled, he at once lectured to them; principles and examples were inexhaustible, all full of novelty—Lan still listened prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: When students gathered he lectured with inexhaustible examples full of novelty, while Lan listened humbly throughout.

sentences.zh: 學者以此益奇之。

translations.literal: Scholars because of this esteemed him all the more strange.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired him all the more for this.

sentences.zh: 而辯能飾非，好為詭說，由是業不久傳。

translations.literal: Yet skilled in debate he could adorn errors and loved strange doctrines; because of this his teaching did not long transmit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was skilled at glossing over errors and loved paradoxical arguments, so his school did not endure.

sentences.zh: 而氣陵牧守，不屈王侯，竟不仕而終。

translations.literal: His spirit overawed provincial governors; he would not bow to princes and marquises, and in the end did not take office but died.
translations.idiomatic: He dominated provincial governors and refused to defer to nobles, dying without ever taking office.

sentences.zh: 劉蘭，武邑人也。

translations.literal: Liu Lan was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lan was from Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，始入小學書《急就篇》。

translations.literal: Past thirty he first entered elementary school to study the Rapid Writing Primer.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty he first studied the Rapid Writing Primer in elementary school.

sentences.zh: 家人覺其聰敏，遂令從師。

translations.literal: His family perceived his intelligence and sharpness and therefore had him follow a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: His family saw his intelligence and sent him to study.

sentences.zh: 受《春秋》、《詩》、《禮》于中山王保安。

translations.literal: He received the Spring and Autumn, Odes, and Rites from Wang Baoan of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Spring and Autumn, Odes, and Rites under Wang Baoan of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 家貧，無以自資，且耕且學。

translations.literal: The family was poor and had no means to support themselves; he both plowed and studied.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and without means, he farmed while he studied.

sentences.zh: 三年之後，便白其兄，求講說。

translations.literal: After three years he told his elder brother he wished to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he told his elder brother he wished to teach.

sentences.zh: 其兄笑而聽之，為立黌舍，聚徒二百。

translations.literal: His brother laughed but consented, built a schoolhouse for him, and gathered two hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: His brother laughed but agreed, built a school, and gathered two hundred students.

sentences.zh: 蘭讀《左氏》，五日一遍，兼能《五經》。

translations.literal: Lan read the Zuo Tradition once every five days and could also master the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Lan read through the Zuo Tradition every five days and mastered the Five Classics as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，張吾貴以聰辯過人，其所解說，不本先儒之旨。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Wugui had surpassed others in cleverness and eloquence, yet his explanations did not rest on the former Confucians' intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wugui had been clever and eloquent, but his teaching did not follow the ancient masters.

sentences.zh: 唯蘭推《經》、《傳》之由，本注者之意，參以緯候及先儒舊事，甚為精悉。

translations.literal: Only Lan traced the classics' and commentaries' origins, based on the original commentators' intent, and compared weaving texts and former Confucians' old affairs—extremely precise and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lan traced the rationale of classics and commentaries, followed the original commentators, and drew on apocryphal and traditional sources with great precision.

sentences.zh: 自後《經》義審博，皆由於蘭。

translations.literal: From then on the meaning of the classics became careful and broad—all because of Lan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on classical interpretation became rigorous and comprehensive, thanks to Lan.

sentences.zh: 蘭又明陰陽，博物多識，故為儒者所宗。

translations.literal: Lan was also clear in yin and yang and broadly knowledgeable in many things; therefore Confucians took him as their patriarch.
translations.idiomatic: He also understood yin-yang lore and many fields of knowledge, and was revered by Confucians.

sentences.zh: 瀛州刺史裴植，征蘭講書于州南館。

translations.literal: Governor Pei Zhi of Yingzhou summoned Lan to lecture at the southern lodge of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Pei Zhi of Yingzhou summoned him to lecture at the provincial southern lodge.

sentences.zh: 植為學主，故生徒甚盛，海內稱焉。

translations.literal: Zhi was master of the school; therefore disciples were very numerous and he was famed within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi served as school master, drawing many students and fame throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又特為中山王英所重。

translations.literal: He was also especially valued by Prince Ying of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was also especially valued by Prince Ying of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 英引在館，令授其子熙、誘、略等。

translations.literal: Ying brought him into his lodge and had him teach his sons Xi, You, and Lüe.
translations.idiomatic: Ying brought him to his residence to teach his sons Xi, You, and Lüe.

sentences.zh: 蘭學徒前後數千，成業者眾。

translations.literal: Lan's disciples before and after numbered in the thousands; those who completed their studies were many.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's students numbered in the thousands over the years, many of whom completed their training.

sentences.zh: 而排毀《公羊》，又非董仲舒，由是見譏於世。

translations.literal: Yet he rejected and slandered the Gongyang and also criticized Dong Zhongshu; because of this he was ridiculed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the Gongyang school and criticized Dong Zhongshu, and was ridiculed for it.

sentences.zh: 為國子助教。

translations.literal: He served as assistant teacher at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant teacher at the National University.

sentences.zh: 靜坐讀書，有人叩門，蘭命引入，葛巾單衣，入與蘭坐，謂曰：「君自是學士，何為每見毀辱？

translations.literal: Sitting quietly reading, when someone knocked at the door Lan had him brought in—a man in hemp headcloth and single garment entered and sat with Lan, saying: "You yourself are a scholar—why are you insulted and humiliated each time?
translations.idiomatic: While reading quietly, someone knocked; Lan admitted a man in hemp cap and plain robe who said: "You are a scholar—why are you constantly insulted?

sentences.zh: 理義長短，竟在誰？

translations.literal: Whether reasoning and principle are long or short, in the end whose are they?
translations.idiomatic: Whether reasoning is right or wrong, whose is it in the end?

sentences.zh: 而過無禮見陵也！

translations.literal: Yet you pass without ritual and are bullied!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you endure such bullying without proper response!

sentences.zh: 今欲相召，當與君正之。」

translations.literal: Now I wish to summon you—I shall set things right with you."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to summon you and set this right with you.

sentences.zh: 言終而出，蘭少時患死。

translations.literal: When the speech ended he went out; Lan soon after died of his illness.
translations.idiomatic: He finished speaking and left; Lan soon died of his illness.

sentences.zh: 孫惠蔚，武邑武遂人也。

translations.literal: Sun Huiwei was a man of Wusui in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huiwei was from Wusui in Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 年十五，粗通《詩》、《書》及《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: At fifteen he roughly mastered the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he had roughly mastered the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 十八，師董道季講《易》。

translations.literal: At eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji.

sentences.zh: 十九，師程玄讀《禮經》及《春秋三傳》。

translations.literal: At nineteen he studied the Book of Rites and the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn under Cheng Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he studied the Rites and the three Spring and Autumn commentaries under Cheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 周流儒肆，有名于冀方。

translations.literal: He traveled through Confucian academies and was famous in the Ji region.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled among Confucian schools and was renowned in Ji.

sentences.zh: 太和初，郡舉孝廉，對策於中書省。

translations.literal: In early Taihe his commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he answered policy questions at the Directorate of Archives.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taihe his commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he took the policy examination at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時中書監高閭因相談薦，俄為中書博士，轉皇宗博士。

translations.literal: At that time Director Gao Lu because of conversation recommended him; soon he became Secretariat Doctor and was transferred to Imperial Clan Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Director Gao Lu recommended him after conversation; he soon became Secretariat Doctor, then Imperial Clan Doctor.

sentences.zh: 閭被敕理定雅樂，惠蔚參其事。

translations.literal: Lu received an edict to arrange the elegant music; Huiwei participated in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was ordered to arrange court music; Huiwei assisted.

sentences.zh: 及樂成，閭上疏請集朝士于太樂，共研是非。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, Lu submitted a memorial requesting court gentlemen assemble at the Grand Music Office to jointly investigate right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was finished, Lu asked court gentlemen to review it at the Grand Music Office.

sentences.zh: 秘書令李彪，自以才辯，立難於其前。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his talent and eloquence, raised difficulties before him.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his eloquence, challenged him.

sentences.zh: 閭命惠蔚與彪抗論，彪不能屈。

translations.literal: Lu ordered Huiwei to debate with Biao; Biao could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu had Huiwei debate Biao, who could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎張彝，常與遊處，每表疏論事，多參訪焉。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Yi often associated with him; whenever memorials discussed affairs, he often consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Yi often consulted him on memorials.

sentences.zh: 十七年，孝文南征，上議告類之禮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he submitted a memorial on the ceremony of reporting to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, during Emperor Xiaowen's southern campaign, he memorialized on reporting rites to ancestors.

sentences.zh: 及太師馮熙薨，惠蔚監其喪禮。

translations.literal: When Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised his mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 上書，令熙未冠之子，皆服成人服。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial that Xi's sons who had not yet capped should all wear adult mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Xi's uncapped sons should wear adult mourning.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚與李彪以儒學相知，及彪位至尚書，惠蔚仍太廟令。

translations.literal: Huiwei and Li Biao knew each other through Confucian learning; when Biao reached Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei and Li Biao were friends in scholarship; when Biao became Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝文曾從容言曰：「道固既登龍門，而孫蔚猶沈涓澮，朕常以為負矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once said at leisure: "Dao Gu has ascended the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei still sinks in a muddy ford—I have always felt this a burden.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once said: "Dao Gu has crossed the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei remains in the mud—I have always regretted this.

sentences.zh: 雖久滯小官，深體通塞，無孜孜之望，儒者以是尚焉。

translations.literal: Though long stuck in minor office, he deeply understood fortune and obstruction and had no eager hopes; Confucians therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Though long in minor posts, he understood fortune and setback without ambition; scholars esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，侍讀東宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as lecturer in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he lectured in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，七廟以平文為太祖。

translations.literal: Earlier the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founder.

sentences.zh: 孝文議定祖宗，以道武為太祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deliberated fixing the ancestors and took Emperor Daowu as Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen fixed Emperor Daowu as Founder.

sentences.zh: 祖宗雖定，然昭穆未改。

translations.literal: Though the ancestors were fixed, the zhao and mu order was not yet changed.
translations.idiomatic: Though ancestors were fixed, the zhao-mu order was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 及孝文崩，將祔神主於廟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, spirit tablets were to be enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen died, spirit tablets were to be installed in the temple.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光兼太常卿，以太祖既改，昭穆以次而易。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, also Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, held that since the Founder was changed, zhao and mu should change in sequence accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, also Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, held that with the Founder changed, zhao-mu should shift accordingly.

sentences.zh: 兼御史中尉、黃門侍郎邢巒，以為太祖雖改，昭穆仍不應易，乃立彈草，欲按奏光。

translations.literal: Concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Luan held that though the Founder was changed, zhao and mu still should not change; he drafted an impeachment to report Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan held that zhao-mu should not change despite the new Founder and drafted impeachment against Guang.

sentences.zh: 光謂惠蔚曰：「此乃禮也，而執法欲見彈劾，思獲助於碩學。」

translations.literal: Guang told Huiwei: "This is ritual law, yet the law officers wish to impeach me—I seek help from a great scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Guang told Huiwei: "This is ritual, yet legal officers wish to impeach me—I need your help.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚曰：「此深得禮變。」

translations.literal: Huiwei said: "This deeply obtains the ritual change."
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei said: "This accords with proper ritual change."

sentences.zh: 尋為書以與光，贊明其事。

translations.literal: Soon he wrote a letter for Guang clarifying the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He soon wrote supporting Guang's position.

sentences.zh: 光以惠蔚書呈宰輔，乃召惠蔚與巒庭議得失。

translations.literal: Guang presented Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers and summoned Huiwei and Luan to court to debate gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Guang presented the letter and summoned Huiwei and Luan to debate at court.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王肅又助巒，而巒理終屈，彈事遂寢。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Su again aided Luan, but Luan's reasoning was ultimately defeated and the impeachment was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Su aided Luan, but Luan lost the debate and the impeachment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位之後，仍在左右，敷訓經典。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanwu succeeded, Huiwei remained at his side expounding the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he remained at court expounding the classics.

sentences.zh: 自冗從僕射遷秘書丞、武邑郡中正。

translations.literal: From Attendant of the Scattered he was moved to Secretariat Assistant and Rectifier of Wuyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Attendant of the Scattered to Secretariat Assistant and Rectifier of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚既入東觀，見典籍未周。

translations.literal: Once Huiwei entered the Eastern Pavilion, he saw the canon was not complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Pavilion he found the canon incomplete.

sentences.zh: 及閱舊典，先無定目，新故雜糅，首尾不全，有者累袠數十，無者曠年不寫。

translations.literal: Reviewing old canons, formerly there was no fixed catalogue; new and old were mixed, beginnings and ends incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Old canons lacked catalogues; new and old were jumbled and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 或篇第剝落，始末淪殘，或文壞字誤，謬爛相屬。

translations.literal: Some volumes had dozens of fascicles; some years had no copying at all.
translations.idiomatic: Some works had dozens of fascicles; others had not been copied for years.

sentences.zh: 卷目雖多，全定者少。

translations.literal: Some fascicles fell apart, beginnings and ends ruined; some texts were damaged and characters wrong, errors and rot piled together.
translations.idiomatic: Some fascicles were damaged, texts corrupt, errors piled up.

sentences.zh: 請依前丞盧昶所撰甲乙新錄，欲裨殘補闕，損並有無，校練句讀，以為定本，次第均寫，永為常式。

translations.literal: Though titles were many, few were wholly correct.
translations.idiomatic: Though titles were numerous, few editions were complete.

sentences.zh: 其省先無本者，廣加推尋，搜求令足。

translations.literal: He requested following former Assistant Lu Chang's A-B New Register to repair gaps, reduce redundancies, collate punctuation, and make a fixed edition copied in order as permanent practice.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed following Lu Chang's catalogue to repair gaps, collate texts, and establish a standard edition.

sentences.zh: 然經記浩博，諸子紛綸，部帙既多，章第紕繆，當非一二校書，歲月可了。

translations.literal: Where the Directorate lacked copies, search widely to make them sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Missing texts should be sought and supplied.

sentences.zh: 求令四門博士及在京儒生四十人，在秘書省專精校考，參定字義。

translations.literal: Yet classics and records are vast and masters numerous—fascicles many and chapters confused; this cannot be finished by one or two collators in a year.
translations.idiomatic: The task was too vast for one or two collators in a year.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: He asked forty Four Gates doctors and capital Confucians to specialize in collation at the Secretariat and fix character meanings.
translations.idiomatic: He requested forty scholars at the Secretariat to collate and fix readings.

sentences.zh: 後為黃門侍郎，代崔光為著作郎。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 才非文史，無所撰著。

translations.literal: Later he became Yellow Gate Gentleman, replacing Cui Guang as Composition Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yellow Gate Gentleman and replaced Cui Guang as Composition Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒、秘書監，仍知史事。

translations.literal: His talent was not in letters and history; he composed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was not literary; he wrote nothing.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，追賞講定之勞，封棗強縣男。

translations.literal: He was moved to Libationer of the National University and Director of the Secretariat, still overseeing historiography.
translations.idiomatic: He became Libationer and Secretariat Director, still overseeing history.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，出為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanchang he was rewarded for fixing the music with enfeoffment as Baron of Zaoqiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang year three he was enfeoffed Baron of Zaoqiang for his work on music.

sentences.zh: 還京，除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In early Mingdi's reign he went out as governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 魏初已來，儒生寒宦，惠蔚最為顯達。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 先單名蔚，正始中，侍講禁內，夜論佛經，有愜帝旨，詔使加「惠」，號惠蔚法師焉。

translations.literal: From early Wei, among cold-office Confucians, Huiwei was most illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: From early Wei, among poor scholars, Huiwei rose highest.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，贈瀛州刺史，諡曰戴。

translations.literal: Earlier his single name was Wei; in Zhengshi, lecturing in the inner palace on Buddhist sutras at night, he pleased the emperor, who ordered "Hui" added—thus the Dharma Master Huiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Wei, he pleased the emperor lecturing on Buddhism at night in Zhengshi and received the added name Hui.

sentences.zh: 子伯禮襲封。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously made governor of Yingzhou with posthumous title Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously governor of Yingzhou, titled Dai.

sentences.zh: 伯禮善隸書，位國子博士。

translations.literal: His son Boli inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boli inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚族曾孫靈暉。

translations.literal: Boli was skilled in clerical script and served as National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Boli excelled in clerical script and served as National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 靈暉少明敏，有器度。

translations.literal: Huiwei's clan great-grandson Linghui.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei's great-grandson by the clan line was Linghui.

sentences.zh: 得惠蔚手錄章疏，研精尋問，更求師友，《三禮》、《三傳》，皆通宗旨。

translations.literal: Linghui was bright and clever young, with capacity and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Linghui was bright and capable from youth.

sentences.zh: 然始就鮑季詳、熊安生質問疑滯，其所發明，熊、鮑無以異也。

translations.literal: Obtaining Huiwei's hand-copied commentaries, he studied them deeply, sought further teachers, and penetrated the gist of the Three Rites and Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Huiwei's manuscripts, sought teachers, and mastered the Three Rites and Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 舉冀州秀才，射策高第。

translations.literal: Recommended as provincial talent of Ji, he ranked high in the target-shooting examination.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Ji talent, he ranked high in the examination.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，累至國子博士，授南陽王綽府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he rose to National University doctor and was appointed Adviser to Prince Chuo of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he became National University doctor and adviser to Prince Chuo of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 綽除定州刺史，仍隨綽之鎮。

translations.literal: When Chuo was made governor of Dingzhou, Linghui followed him to the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo became governor of Dingzhou, Linghui followed him.

sentences.zh: 所為猖蹶，靈暉唯默默憂悴，不能諫止。

translations.literal: Chuo's conduct was reckless; Linghui only silently grieved and could not remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo behaved recklessly; Linghui grieved silently and could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 綽表請靈暉為王師，以管記馬子結為諮議。

translations.literal: Chuo memorialized requesting Linghui as Prince's Master and registrar Ma Zijie as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo requested Linghui as Prince's Master and Ma Zijie as adviser.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以王師三品，奏啟不合。

translations.literal: The court held that Prince's Master was third rank and the memorial did not conform.
translations.idiomatic: The court held Prince's Master was third rank and the request improper.

sentences.zh: 後主於啟下手詔云：「但用之。」

translations.literal: The Later Lord wrote on the memorial: "Use him anyway."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote on the memorial: "Use him anyway.

sentences.zh: 儒者甚以為榮。

translations.literal: Confucians greatly took this as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians took this as great honor.

sentences.zh: 綽除大將軍，靈暉以王師領大將軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Chuo was made Grand General, Linghui as Prince's Master also headed the Grand General's secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo became Grand General, Linghui as Prince's Master headed his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 綽誅，停廢。

translations.literal: When Chuo was executed, Linghui was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo was executed, Linghui was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 從綽死後，每至七日至百日，靈暉恆為綽請僧設齋行道。

translations.literal: After Chuo's death, on each seventh day up to the hundredth day Linghui always requested monks to set vegetarian feasts and perform rites for Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuo's death, Linghui arranged Buddhist rites on the seventh days through the hundredth day.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，卒。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, he died.

sentences.zh: 馬子結者，其先扶風人，世仕涼土，魏太和中入洛。

translations.literal: Ma Zijie—his ancestors were men of Fufeng who for generations served in the Liang lands; in the Taihe era of Wei they entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zijie was descended from Fufeng families who had long served in the northwest; his line entered Luoyang in the Wei Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 父祖俱清官。

translations.literal: Father and grandfathers were all pure officials.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfathers had all held clean offices.

sentences.zh: 子結及兄子廉、子尚三人，皆涉文學。

translations.literal: Zijie and his elder brother's sons Lian and Shang—all three were versed in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Zijie and his nephews Lian and Shang were all accomplished in literature.

sentences.zh: 陽休之牧西兗，子廉、子尚、子結與諸朝士各有贈詩。

translations.literal: When Yang Xiuzhi governed western Yan, Lian, Shang, and Zijie each presented poems with other court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xiuzhi governed western Yan, the three each exchanged poems with other courtiers.

sentences.zh: 陽總為一篇酬答。

translations.literal: Yang composed one piece in reply altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Yang replied with a single poem for all of them.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「三馬皆白眉」者也。

translations.literal: The poem says: "The three horses all have white brows."
translations.idiomatic: The poem runs: "All three horses have white brows."

sentences.zh: 子結為南陽王綽管記，隨綽定州。

translations.literal: Zijie served as registrar for Prince Chuo of Nanyang and followed Chuo to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zijie was registrar to Prince Chuo of Nanyang and accompanied him to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 綽每出遊獵，必令子結走馬從禽。

translations.literal: Whenever Chuo went out hunting, he always had Zijie gallop after the game.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chuo hunted, he made Zijie ride after the quarry.

sentences.zh: 子結既儒緩，衣垂帽落，或叫或啼，令騎驅之，非墜馬不止。

translations.literal: Zijie was by nature slow and scholarly; his robes trailed and his cap slipped, and he would shout or cry until riders drove him on—not stopping until he nearly fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Slow and bookish, robes trailing and cap askew, he would shout until attendants drove his horse on, nearly throwing him each time.

sentences.zh: 綽以為笑。

translations.literal: Chuo found it amusing.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo found this hilarious.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見親狎，啟為諮議焉。

translations.literal: Because of this he was gradually treated with intimacy and was recommended as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually won Chuo's favor and was made adviser.

sentences.zh: 石曜字白曜，中山安善人。

translations.literal: Shi Yao, styled Baiyao, was a man of Anshan in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yao, courtesy name Baiyao, was from Anshan in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 亦以儒學進，居官清儉。

translations.literal: He also advanced through Confucian learning and in office was pure and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: He too rose through scholarship and lived frugally in office.

sentences.zh: 武平中，為黎陽郡守。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era he was governor of Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuping he governed Liyang.

sentences.zh: 時丞相咸陽王世子斛律武都出為兗州刺史，性貪暴。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince of the Duke of Xianyang, Hulu Wu of the Prime Minister's house, went out as governor of Yanzhou—greedy and violent by nature.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince of Duke Xianyang, Hulu Wu, became governor of Yanzhou—a greedy and brutal man.

sentences.zh: 先過衛縣，令丞以下，斂絹數千疋遺之。

translations.literal: Passing through Wei county first, he extorted several thousand bolts of silk from the magistrate, assistant, and those below.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Wei county, he squeezed thousands of bolts of silk from local officials.

sentences.zh: 至黎陽，令左右諷動曜及縣官。

translations.literal: Arriving at Liyang, he had his attendants hint to Yao and the county officials.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang he had his men pressure Yao and the county staff.

sentences.zh: 曜手持一絹謂武都曰：「此是老石機杼，聊以奉贈。

translations.literal: Yao held one bolt of silk and told Wu: "This is from old Shi's loom—I offer it in gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yao held up one bolt and said: "This is from my own loom—a small gift.

sentences.zh: 自此以外，並須出於吏人。

translations.literal: Beyond this, all must come from clerks and the people.
translations.idiomatic: Anything more must come from your officials and the people.

sentences.zh: 吏人之物，一毫不敢輒犯。」

translations.literal: Of the people's goods, not a hair may I presumptuously touch.
translations.idiomatic: I will not touch a penny that belongs to the people.

sentences.zh: 武都亦知曜清素純儒，笑而不責。

translations.literal: Wu also knew Yao was pure and a pure Confucian; he laughed and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu knew Yao was incorruptible and laughed it off.

sentences.zh: 曜著《石子》十卷，言甚淺俗。

translations.literal: Yao composed The Stone Master in ten chapters—its words very plain and popular.
translations.idiomatic: Yao wrote The Stone Master in ten chapters, in plain language.

sentences.zh: 位終譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as governor of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died as governor of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 靈暉子萬壽，字仙期，一字遐年。

translations.literal: Linghui's son Wanshou, styled Xianqi, also styled Xianian.
translations.idiomatic: Linghui's son Wanshou, courtesy names Xianqi and Xianian.

sentences.zh: 聰識機警，博涉經史，善屬文，美譚笑。

translations.literal: Clever, perceptive, and quick, he ranged broadly through classics and histories, was skilled at composition, and delightful in wit.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and well read, he wrote well and sparkled in conversation.

sentences.zh: 在齊，仕為陽休之開府行參軍。

translations.literal: Under Qi he served as acting aide in Yang Xiuzhi's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he served on Yang Xiuzhi's staff.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝受禪，滕穆王引為文學。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Prince Teng of Mu summoned him as literary attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui took the throne, Prince Teng made him a literary aide.

sentences.zh: 坐衣冠不整，配防江南。

translations.literal: Because his dress was not in order, he was assigned to garrison the south.
translations.idiomatic: For improper dress he was sent to garrison the south.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管宇文述，召典軍書。

translations.literal: The campaign general Yuwen Shu summoned him to manage military documents.
translations.idiomatic: General Yuwen Shu put him in charge of military correspondence.

sentences.zh: 萬壽本自書生，從容文雅，一旦從軍，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Wanshou was originally a bookish man, easy and refined; suddenly entering the army, he was depressed and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar thrust into the army, he grew depressed and bitter.

sentences.zh: 為五言詩贈京邑知友。

translations.literal: He composed a five-character poem and sent it to friends in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a pentasyllabic poem to friends in the capital.

sentences.zh: 詩至京，盛為當時吟誦，天下好事者，多書壁上而玩之。

translations.literal: When the poem reached the capital it was widely chanted; men of taste throughout the realm copied it on walls to enjoy.
translations.idiomatic: The poem swept the capital; enthusiasts copied it on walls everywhere.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，十餘年不得調。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district and for more than ten years received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and went unrewarded for over a decade.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，拜豫章王長史，非其好也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was made chief steward to the Prince of Yuzhang—not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: At Renshou he became chief steward to the Prince of Yuzhang, a post he disliked.

sentences.zh: 王轉封于齊，即為齊王文學。

translations.literal: When the prince was transferred and enfeoffed in Qi, Wanshou became literary attendant to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to Qi, Wanshou became his literary attendant.

sentences.zh: 當時，諸王官屬，多被夷滅，由是彌不自安，因謝病免。

translations.literal: At that time many staff of the princes were exterminated; he grew all the more uneasy and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial brothers' staffs were slaughtered, he quit on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，授大理司直，卒於官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made direct judge of the Court of Review and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made direct judge of the Court of Review and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten chapters circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in ten chapters circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 徐遵明，字子判，華陰人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zunming, styled Zipan, was a man of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zunming, courtesy name Zipan, was from Huayin.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，好學，年十七，隨鄉人毛靈和等詣山東求學。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he loved learning; at seventeen he followed fellow townsman Mao Linghe and others east of the mountains to seek learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and studious, at seventeen he went east with Mao Linghe to study.

sentences.zh: 至上党，乃師屯留王聰，受《毛詩》、《尚書》、《禮記》。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangdang, he studied under Wang Cong of Tunliu and received the Mao Odes, Documents, and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangdang he studied the Mao Odes, Documents, and Rites under Wang Cong.

sentences.zh: 一年，便辭聰游燕、趙，師事張吾貴。

translations.literal: After one year he left Cong and traveled through Yan and Zhao, taking Zhang Wugui as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he left for Yan and Zhao to study under Zhang Wugui.

sentences.zh: 吾貴門徒甚盛。

translations.literal: Wugui's disciples were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui had a huge following.

sentences.zh: 遵明伏膺數月，乃私謂友人曰：「張生名高而義無檢格，凡所講說，不愜吾心。

translations.literal: Zunming attended reverently for several months, then privately told a friend: "Master Zhang's fame is high but his conduct lacks restraint; all he expounds fails to satisfy my heart.
translations.idiomatic: After months he told a friend: "Zhang is famous but undisciplined; his lectures do not satisfy me.

sentences.zh: 請更從師。」

translations.literal: I beg to find another teacher.
translations.idiomatic: I must find another master.

sentences.zh: 遂與平原田猛略就范陽孫買德。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Tian Menglue of Pingyuan he went to Sun Maide of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Tian Menglue to study under Sun Maide of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 受業一年，復欲去之。

translations.literal: After one year of receiving instruction he wished to leave again.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he wished to leave again.

sentences.zh: 猛略謂遵明曰：「君年少從師，每不終業，如此用意，終恐無成。」

translations.literal: Menglue told Zunming: "You are young and follow teachers yet never finish a course—with such intent you will surely never succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Menglue warned him that skipping masters would leave him unfinished.

sentences.zh: 遵明乃指其心曰：「吾今知真師所在矣，正在於此。」

translations.literal: Zunming pointed to his heart and said: "I now know where the true teacher is—it is right here."
translations.idiomatic: Zunming pointed to his heart: "My true teacher is here."

sentences.zh: 乃詣平原唐遷，居於蠶舍，讀《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《尚書》、《三禮》。

translations.literal: He then went to Tang Qian of Pingyuan and dwelt in a silkworm shed, reading the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, Documents, and Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Tang Qian in a silkworm shed for six years, mastering the core classics.

sentences.zh: 不出門院，凡經六年，時彈箏吹笛，以自娛慰。

translations.literal: Not leaving the courtyard gate, altogether six years; at times he played zither and flute to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: He rarely left the courtyard, amusing himself with music.

sentences.zh: 又知陽平館陶趙世業家有《服氏春秋》，是晉世永嘉舊寫。

translations.literal: He also knew that Zhao Shiye of Guantao in Yangping had the Fu school's Spring and Autumn—an old copy from the Yongjia era of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He learned that Zhao Shiye possessed an old Fu-school Spring and Autumn from the Jin Yongjia era.

sentences.zh: 遵明乃往讀之，復經數載。

translations.literal: Zunming went to read it and spent several more years.
translations.idiomatic: He read it for several more years.

sentences.zh: 因手撰《春秋義章》，為三十卷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally composed Meaning and Chapters of the Spring and Autumn in thirty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote Meaning and Chapters of the Spring and Autumn in thirty chapters.

sentences.zh: 是後教授門徒，每臨講坐，先持執疏，然後敷講。

translations.literal: Afterward when he taught disciples, each time he took his seat to lecture he first held his commentary and then expounded.
translations.idiomatic: When lecturing he always held his commentary before expounding.

sentences.zh: 學徒至今，浸以成俗。

translations.literal: Disciples to this day have gradually made it custom.
translations.idiomatic: His students made this a lasting custom.

sentences.zh: 遵明講學於外，二十餘年，海內莫不宗仰。

translations.literal: Zunming lectured abroad for more than twenty years; within the seas none did not look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: For over twenty years he taught abroad, revered throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 頗好聚斂，與劉獻之、張吾貴皆河北聚徒教授，懸納絲粟，留衣物以待之，名曰影質，有損儒者之風。

translations.literal: He quite loved amassing wealth; with Liu Xianzhi and Zhang Wugui he all gathered disciples to teach in Hebei, collecting silk and grain in advance and keeping clothes as pledge—called "shadow pledge," damaging Confucian wind.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved wealth, like Liu Xianzhi and Zhang Wugui collecting fees and pledges—a practice that tarnished scholarly dignity.

sentences.zh: 遵明見鄭玄《論語序》云「書以八寸策」，誤作「八十宗」，因曲為之說。

translations.literal: Zunming saw in Zheng Xuan's Analects preface "writings use eight-inch bamboo slips" but misread it as "eighty clans" and twisted a explanation for it.
translations.idiomatic: He misread Zheng Xuan's "eight-inch slips" as "eighty clans" and twisted an explanation.

sentences.zh: 其僻也皆如此。

translations.literal: His eccentricities were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His eccentricities were typical.

sentences.zh: 獻之、吾貴又甚焉。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and Wugui were even worse.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and Wugui were worse still.

sentences.zh: 遵明不好京輦，以兗州有舊，因徙屬焉。

translations.literal: Zunming disliked the capital region; because Yanzhou was his old home he transferred his household allegiance there.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked the capital and moved his household registration to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，任城太守李湛將舉義兵，遵明同其事。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Li Zhan, governor of Rencheng, was about to raise righteous troops; Zunming joined his cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Zunming joined Li Zhan's uprising.

sentences.zh: 夜至人間，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: At night he went among the people and was killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by mutinous soldiers at night.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，遵明弟子通直散騎侍郎李業興表求加策命，卒無贈諡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, his disciple Regular Attendant Li Yexing memorialized requesting posthumous titles; in the end there was no grant or posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year two his disciple Li Yexing sought posthumous honors for him, but none were granted.

sentences.zh: 董徵，字文發，頓丘衛國人也。

translations.literal: Dong Zheng, styled Wenfa, was a man of Dunqiu in Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zheng, courtesy name Wenfa, was from Dunqiu in Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺二寸，好古學，尚雅素。

translations.literal: Seven chi two inches in height, he loved antiquity and learning and esteemed elegance and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and fond of antiquity, he valued plain elegance.

sentences.zh: 年十七，師清河監伯陽受《論語》、《毛詩》、《春秋》、《周易》，河內高望崇受《周官》，後於博陵劉獻之遍受諸經。

translations.literal: At seventeen he studied the Analects, Mao Odes, Spring and Autumn, and Changes under Jian Boyang of Qinghe; the Offices of Zhou under Gao Wangchong of Henei; later under Liu Xianzhi of Boling he received all the classics comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he studied under several masters and with Liu Xianzhi mastered the canon.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，大義精練，講授生徒。

translations.literal: Within several years he refined the great meanings and lectured to students.
translations.idiomatic: Within years he mastered the essentials and began teaching.

sentences.zh: 太和末，為四門小學博士。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe he was doctor at the Four Gates Elementary School.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe he taught at the Four Gates school.

sentences.zh: 後宣武詔徵入ＩＹ華宮，令孫惠蔚問以《六經》。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xuanwu ordered him summoned to the Hua Palace and had Sun Huiwei question him on the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu summoned him to the Hua Palace for examination by Sun Huiwei on the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 仍詔徵教授京兆、清河、廣平、汝南四王。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Zheng to teach the princes of Jingzhao, Qinghe, Guangping, and Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to instruct four imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 後累遷安州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly moved to governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵因述職，路次過家，置酒高會，大享邑老。

translations.literal: Zheng took advantage of a mission to pass his home, set out wine for a grand gathering, and greatly feasted the elders of his district.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home on duty, he feasted the elders of his district.

sentences.zh: 乃言曰：「腰龜返國，昔人稱榮，仗節還家，雲胡不樂。」

translations.literal: He then said: "Waist tortoise, returning to one's state—men of old called it glory; bearing the staff home—why not rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: He said: "To return home with rank is glory—why should I not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 因誡二三子弟曰：「此之富貴，匪自天降，乃勤學所致耳。」

translations.literal: He admonished several younger kinsmen: "This wealth and honor did not fall from heaven—it came from diligent study."
translations.idiomatic: He told his nephews: "This honor came from study, not from heaven."

sentences.zh: 時人榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the time honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors admired him.

sentences.zh: 入為司農少卿、光祿大夫，後以老解職。

translations.literal: He entered office as Vice Minister of Agriculture and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; later he resigned on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Agriculture and Grand Master, then retired.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongxi year two.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝以徵昔授學業，故優贈儀同三司、尚書左僕射、相州刺史，諡曰文烈。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, because Zheng had formerly taught him, therefore generously posthumously made him equal to the third rank, Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing, governor of Xiangzhou, with posthumous title Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored him for having been his teacher.

sentences.zh: 子仲曜。

translations.literal: His son Zhongyao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhongyao.

sentences.zh: 李業興，上党長子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yexing was a man of Changzi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing was from Changzi in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 祖虯、父玄紀，並以儒學舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jiu and father Xuanji were both recommended as filial and incorrupt through Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather and father were both filial-incorrupt scholars.

sentences.zh: 玄紀卒于金鄉令。

translations.literal: Xuanji died while magistrate of Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father died as magistrate of Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 業興少耿介志學，晚乃師事徐遵明于趙、魏之間。

translations.literal: Yexing was upright and studious from youth; only later did he follow Xu Zunming as teacher between Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and studious from youth, he later studied under Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 時有漁陽鮮于靈馥亦聚徒教授，而遵明聲譽未高，著錄尚寡。

translations.literal: At that time Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang also gathered disciples to teach, but Zunming's reputation was not yet high and his register was still small.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Lingfu also taught, but Zunming was not yet famous.

sentences.zh: 業興乃詣靈馥黌舍，類受業者。

translations.literal: Yexing therefore went to Lingfu's school and sat among the students.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing visited Lingfu's school disguised among the students.

sentences.zh: 靈馥乃謂曰：「李生久逐羌博士，何所得也？」

translations.literal: Lingfu told him: "Master Li has long chased the Qiang doctor—what have you gained?
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu mocked him for studying with the "Qiang doctor" Xu.

sentences.zh: 業興默爾不言。

translations.literal: Yexing was silent and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 及靈馥說《左傳》，業興問其大義數條，靈馥不能對。

translations.literal: When Lingfu lectured on the Zuo Tradition, Yexing asked several great meanings; Lingfu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingfu lectured on the Zuo, Yexing stumped him on major points.

sentences.zh: 於是振衣而起曰：「羌弟子正如此耳！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he shook out his robes, rose, and said: "A Qiang disciple is just like this!
translations.idiomatic: He rose and said: "So much for the Qiang master's disciple!

sentences.zh: 遂便徑還。

translations.literal: And at once went straight back.
translations.idiomatic: And walked out.

sentences.zh: 自此，靈馥生徒傾學而就遵明。

translations.literal: From this Lingfu's disciples all shifted their studies to Zunming.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu's students deserted him for Zunming.

sentences.zh: 學徒大盛，業興之為也。

translations.literal: Disciples greatly flourished—this was Yexing's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming's school flourished because of Yexing.

sentences.zh: 後乃博涉百家，圖緯、風角、天文、占候，無不討練。

translations.literal: Later he ranged broadly through the hundred masters, charts and weft texts, wind angles, astronomy, and divination—nothing not investigated and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: He later mastered divination, astronomy, and the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 尤長算曆。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 雖在貧賤，常自矜負，若禮待不足，縱於權貴，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Though in poverty and baseness, he often prided himself; if ritual treatment was insufficient, even toward the powerful he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, he was proud and would not bow to the powerful without proper respect.

sentences.zh: 後為王遵業門客。

translations.literal: Later he became a client of Wang Zunye.
translations.idiomatic: He later became retainer to Wang Zunye.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為校書郎。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he served as collation gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he became collation gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以世行趙匪曆，節氣後辰下算。

translations.literal: Because the era followed the Zhao calendar with errors, the solar terms lagged behind the lower chen in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court calendar followed the faulty Zhao system, seasonal nodes were miscalculated.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，業興乃為《戊子元曆》上之。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era Yexing then presented the Wuzi Calendar to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanchang era he presented the Wuzi Calendar to the throne.

sentences.zh: 于時屯騎校尉張洪、蕩寇將軍張龍詳等九家，各獻新曆。

translations.literal: At that time nine houses including Cavalry Commandant Zhang Hong and General Who Quells Bandits Zhang Longxiang each presented new calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Nine scholars including Zhang Hong and Zhang Longxiang each submitted new calendars.

sentences.zh: 宣武詔令共為一曆。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu ordered them to make one calendar together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu ordered them unified into one calendar.

sentences.zh: 洪等後遂共推業興為主，成《戊子曆》，正光三年，奏行之。

translations.literal: Hong and the others later jointly made Yexing master; they completed the Wuzi Calendar, and in the third year of Zhengguang it was memorialized and put into use.
translations.idiomatic: They made Yexing lead the work; the Wuzi Calendar was completed and adopted in Zhengguang year three.

sentences.zh: 業興以殷曆甲寅，黃帝辛卯，徒有積元，術數亡缺。

translations.literal: Yexing held that the Yin calendar's jiazi and the Yellow Emperor's xinmao had only accumulated origins while computational methods lacked and were defective.
translations.idiomatic: He argued prior calendars had flawed computational foundations.

sentences.zh: 又修之，各為一卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: He revised them, each in one chapter, and transmitted them in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He revised them in separate chapters that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 建義初，敕典儀注。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was ordered to oversee ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyi's start he oversaw court ritual.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除著作郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Composition Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Composition Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，以前造曆之勳，賜爵長子伯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, for his former merit in making the calendar, he was granted the title Baron of Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an year three he was enfeoffed Baron of Changzi for the calendar work.

sentences.zh: 後以孝武帝登極之初，豫行禮事，封屯留縣子，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's accession, for participating in inaugural rites he was enfeoffed Viscount of Tunliu and made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Viscount of Tunliu for rites at Xiaowu's accession.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年二月，孝武帝釋奠，業興與魏季景、溫子升、竇瑗為摘句。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Yongxi, when Emperor Xiaowu performed the libation ceremony, Yexing with Wei Jijing, Wen Zisheng, and Dou Yuan made selected passages.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year three he joined the libation ceremony as a commentator.

sentences.zh: 後入為侍讀。

translations.literal: Later he entered as lecturer-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He later became lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴之始，起部郎中辛術奏：「今皇居徙禦，百度創始，營構一興，必宜中制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the move to Ye, Director of the Ministry of Rites Xin Shu memorialized: "Now the imperial residence shifts; all measures are newly founded—once construction rises, standards must be set centrally.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Ye, Xin Shu urged central standards for the new capital.

sentences.zh: 李業興碩學通儒，博聞多識，萬門千戶，所宜詢訪。

translations.literal: Li Yexing is a great scholar and penetrating Confucian, broadly heard and much knowing—the myriad gates and thousand households should consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing, a leading scholar, should be consulted on the new capital.

sentences.zh: 今求就之披圖案記，考定是非，參古雜今，折中為制。」

translations.literal: Now I request he come to spread out maps and records, examine and fix right and wrong, compare ancient with present, and strike the mean as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He should collate maps and records to set regulations blending past and present.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 于時尚書右僕射、營構大匠高隆之被詔繕修三署樂器、衣服及百戲之屬，乃奏請業興共事。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of the Right and Grand Master of Construction Gao Longzhi was ordered to repair the three directorates' musical instruments, robes, and the hundred entertainments; he memorialized requesting Yexing share the work.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi had Yexing help repair palace instruments and regalia.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，與兼散騎常侍李諧、兼吏部郎盧元明使梁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping, together with Concurrent Regular Attendant Li Xie and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Yuanming he was envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year four he was envoy to Liang with Li Xie and Lu Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 梁散騎常侍硃異問業興曰：「魏洛中委粟山是南郊邪？

translations.literal: Liang Regular Attendant Zhu Yi asked Yexing: "Is Wei's Luoyang Mount Weisu the southern suburb?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi asked whether Mount Weisu in Luoyang was the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 圓丘邪？」

translations.literal: Or the round mound?
translations.idiomatic: Or the round altar?

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「委粟是圓丘，非南郊。」

translations.literal: Yexing said: "Weisu is the round mound, not the southern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said it was the round altar, not the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「比聞郊、丘異所，是用鄭義。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Recently I heard the suburban altar and mound differ in place—this uses the Zheng interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said Liang followed Wang's interpretation instead of Zheng's.

sentences.zh: 我此中用王義。」

translations.literal: We here use Wang's interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: We use Wang's view here.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「然。

translations.literal: Yexing said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing agreed.

sentences.zh: 洛京郊丘之處，用鄭解。」

translations.literal: The place of suburban altar and mound in Luoyang uses Zheng's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang ritual sites followed Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「若然，女子逆降傍親，亦從鄭以不？」

translations.literal: Yi said: "If so, when women marry down to collateral kin, do you also follow Zheng?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked whether women's marriage rules also followed Zheng.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「此之一事，亦不專從。

translations.literal: Yexing said: "In this one matter we do not exclusively follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said they did not follow Zheng exclusively on that point.

sentences.zh: 若卿此間用王義，除禫應用二十五月，何以王儉《喪禮》，禫用二十七月也？」

translations.literal: If your side uses Wang, for removing mourning should you use twenty-five months—why does Wang Jian's Mourning Rites use twenty-seven for the final mourning period?"
translations.idiomatic: He challenged Liang's mourning practice using Wang Jian's twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 異遂不答。

translations.literal: Yi then did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fell silent.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「我昨見明堂，四柱方屋，都無五九之室，當是裴頠所制。

translations.literal: Yexing said: "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall—four pillars and a square house, entirely without the five-by-nine chambers; it must be Pei Yan's design.
translations.idiomatic: He noted the Bright Hall lacked the traditional five-by-nine chambers of Pei Yan's design.

sentences.zh: 明堂上圓下方，裴唯除室耳，今此上不圓，何也？」

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers—yet this top is not round; why?
translations.idiomatic: He asked why the hall was not round on top as ritual required.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「圓方俗說，經典無文，何怪于方。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Round and square are vulgar sayings; the classics have no text—why wonder at square?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi dismissed round-and-square as folk belief without classical warrant.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「圓方之言，出處甚明，卿自不見。

translations.literal: Yexing said: "The words round and square have very clear origins—you yourself do not see them.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the classics clearly supported round and square.

sentences.zh: 見卿錄梁主《孝經義》亦云'上圓下方'，卿言豈非自相矛盾？」

translations.literal: I see your recorded Liang ruler's Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety also says 'round above, square below'—are your words not self-contradictory?"
translations.idiomatic: He cited Liang's own commentary contradicting Yi.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「若然，圓方竟出何經？」

translations.literal: Yi said: "If so, from what classic do round and square ultimately come?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked for the source.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「出《孝經援神契》。」

translations.literal: Yexing said: "From the Classic of Filial Piety Apocryphal Divine Contract."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cited the Filial Piety apocryphon.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「緯候之書，何可信也！」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Weft and omen books—how can they be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi rejected apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「卿若不信，《靈威仰》、《葉光紀》之類，經典亦無出者，卿復信不？」

translations.literal: Yexing said: "If you do not believe them, books like Spiritual Majesty and Leaf Light Annals also have no classical source—do you believe those?"
translations.idiomatic: Yexing countered that Liang used other texts without classical sources too.

sentences.zh: 異不答。

translations.literal: Yi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi again was silent.

sentences.zh: 梁武問業興：「《詩·周南》，王者之風，系之周公；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Yexing: "In the Odes, Zhou South is the king's wind, attached to the Duke of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu asked about the Zhou and Shao sections of the Odes.

sentences.zh: 《召南》，仁賢之風，系之召公。

translations.literal: Shao South is the humane and worthy wind, attached to the Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao South was attached to the Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 何名為系？」

translations.literal: What is meant by 'attached'?"
translations.idiomatic: What does 'attached' mean?

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「鄭注《儀禮》云：昔太王、王季居於岐陽，躬行《召南》之教以興王業。

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "Zheng's note on the Ceremonial says: Formerly Grandfather Tai and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally practiced Shao South's teaching to raise the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Zheng Xuan on the dukes of Zhou and Shao.

sentences.zh: 及文王行今《周南》之教以受命，作邑於酆。

translations.literal: When King Wen practiced present Zhou South's teaching to receive the Mandate, he made his seat at Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Wen received the Mandate at Feng through Zhou South.

sentences.zh: 文王為諸侯之地所化之國，今既登九五之尊，不可復守諸侯之地，故分封二公，名為系。」

translations.literal: Wen was lord of the lands transformed by feudal states; now having ascended to the nine-five dignity he could not again keep feudal lands—therefore he enfeoffed the two dukes, named 'attached.'
translations.idiomatic: Wen enfeoffed the two dukes, hence 'attached.'

sentences.zh: 梁武又問：「《尚書》'正月上日，受終文祖'，此時何正？」

translations.literal: The Liang ruler also asked: "In the Documents 'first month, first day, received the end from the culture-ancestor'—what calendar month was this?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked which month the Documents passage meant.

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「此夏正月。」

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "This is the first month of summer."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the summer first month.

sentences.zh: 梁武言：「何以得知？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "How do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how he knew.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「案《尚書中候運衡篇》雲'日月營始'，故知夏正。」

translations.literal: Yexing said: "According to the Documents apocryphon Transport Balance it says 'sun and moon begin their circuit'—thus I know it is summer's first month."
translations.idiomatic: He cited an apocryphon on the solar cycle.

sentences.zh: 又問：「堯時以前，何月為正？」

translations.literal: He also asked: "Before Yao, what month was taken as first?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked what calendar preceded Yao.

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「自堯以上，書典不載，實所不知。」

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "From above Yao, books and canons are not recorded—I truly do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said records before Yao did not say.

sentences.zh: 梁武又云：「'寅賓出日'，是正月，'日中星鳥，以殷仲春'，即是二月。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler also said: "'Guest at sunrise' is the first month; 'sun at mid-day, stars like birds, marking mid-spring of Yin' is the second month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cited the Canon of Yao.

sentences.zh: 此出《堯典》，何得雲堯時不知用何正？」

translations.literal: This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can you say Yao's time did not know what calendar was used?
translations.idiomatic: He challenged Yexing's claim of ignorance.

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「雖三正不同，言時節者，皆據夏時正月。

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "Though the three calendars differ, when speaking of seasons all rely on summer's first month.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said seasonal language used the Xia first month.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》：'仲春二月，會男女之無夫家者。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou: 'mid-spring second month, gather men and women without spouses.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Zhou Rites.

sentences.zh: '雖自周書，月亦夏時。

translations.literal: Though from Zhou's book, the month is also summer time.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhou texts used Xia months.

sentences.zh: 堯之日月，亦當如此。

translations.literal: Yao's sun and moon should be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's calendar should be the same.

sentences.zh: 但所見不深，無以辯析明問。」

translations.literal: But what I have seen is not deep enough to analyze your clear questions.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted he could not fully answer.

sentences.zh: 梁武又曰：「《禮》：原壤母死，叩木而歌。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler also said: "In the Rites, when Yuan Rang's mother died, he knocked wood and sang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about Yuan Rang in the Rites.

sentences.zh: 孔子聖人，而與壤為友？」

translations.literal: Confucius was a sage—yet he befriended Rang?
translations.idiomatic: Why would Confucius befriend him?

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「孔即自解，言親者不失其親，故者不失其故。」

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "Confucius himself explained: those close do not lose the close; the old do not lose the old."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cited Confucius on keeping old ties.

sentences.zh: 又問：「壤何處人？」

translations.literal: He also asked: "What place was Rang from?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Rang's origin.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《注》云：原壤，孔子幼之舊故。

translations.literal: He replied: "The note says Yuan Rang was Confucius's childhood old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says he was Confucius's childhood friend.

sentences.zh: 是魯人。」

translations.literal: He was a man of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was from Lu.

sentences.zh: 又問：「原壤不孝，有逆人倫，何以存故舊之小節，廢不孝之大罪？」

translations.literal: He also asked: "Yuan Rang was unfilial and violated human relations—why keep a small tie of old acquaintance and abandon the great crime of unfiliality?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked why Confucius kept an unfilial friend.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「原壤所行，事自彰著，幼少之交，非是今始。

translations.literal: He replied: "Yuan Rang's conduct was self-evident; the childhood tie was not begun now.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the tie was old and Rang's faults were known.

sentences.zh: 既無大故，何容棄之？」

translations.literal: Since there was no great breach, how could he be cast off?
translations.idiomatic: Without grave cause Confucius would not cast him off.

sentences.zh: 又問：「孔子聖人，何以書原壤之事，垂法萬代？」

translations.literal: He also asked: "Confucius was a sage—why record Yuan Rang's affair to set law for ten thousand generations?"
translations.idiomatic: Why record it for posterity?

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「此是後人所錄，非孔子自製，猶合葬於防。

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "This was recorded by later men, not made by Confucius himself—like joint burial at Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said later editors recorded it, as with other Rites passages.

sentences.zh: 如此 之比，《禮記》之中，動有百數。」

translations.literal: Matters like this in the Book of Rites number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases number in the hundreds in the Rites.

sentences.zh: 又問：「《易》有太極，極是有無？」

translations.literal: He also asked: "The Changes has the Supreme Ultimate—is the ultimate being or non-being?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether the Supreme Ultimate was being or non-being.

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：「所傳太極是有。」

translations.literal: Yexing replied: "The transmitted Supreme Ultimate is being."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the Supreme Ultimate exists.

sentences.zh: 還，兼散騎常侍，加中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Returning, he was Concurrent Regular Attendant and made Grand General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Concurrent Regular Attendant and Central Army general.

sentences.zh: 業興家世農夫，雖學殖，而舊音不改。

translations.literal: Yexing's family for generations were farmers; though learned, his old accent did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Though learned, he kept his rural accent.

sentences.zh: 梁武問其宗門多少，答曰：「薩四十家。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked how many in his clan; he answered: "Forty Sa households.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about his clan, he said forty households.

sentences.zh: 使還，孫騰謂曰：「何意為吳兒所笑！」

translations.literal: When sent back, Sun Teng told him: "How could you let those Wu fellows laugh at you!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng scolded him for being mocked in Liang.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「業興猶被笑，試遣公去，當著被罵。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If Yexing is still laughed at, try sending you—you would surely be cursed."
translations.idiomatic: He replied Sun Teng would fare worse.

sentences.zh: 邢子才云：「爾婦疾‰，或問實耶？」

translations.literal: Xing Zicai said: "Your wife is ill—or is it real?"
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai joked about his wife's illness.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「爾大癡！

translations.literal: Yexing said: "You're a great fool!
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cursed him.

sentences.zh: 但道此，人疑者半，信者半，誰檢看？」

translations.literal: Just say this—half will doubt, half believe; who will check?"
translations.idiomatic: Say that and half will believe without checking."

sentences.zh: 武定元年，除國子祭酒，仍侍讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuding he was appointed Libationer of the National University and still served as lecturer-in-reading.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding 1 he was made Libationer of the National University and continued as lecturer-in-reading.

sentences.zh: 神武以業興明術數，軍行常問焉。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because Yexing was skilled in numerology and divination, often consulted him on military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yexing was skilled in numerology, Shenwu often consulted him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 業興曰某日某處勝，謂所親曰：「彼若告勝，自然賞吾；

translations.literal: Yexing would say that on such-and-such a day at such-and-such a place there would be victory, and told those close to him: "If they report victory, they will naturally reward me;
translations.idiomatic: Yexing would predict victory for a given day and place, and told intimates, "If they report victory, they will reward me;

sentences.zh: 彼若凶敗，安能罪吾？」

translations.literal: if there is defeat, how can they blame me?"
translations.idiomatic: if there is defeat, how can they blame me?"

sentences.zh: 芒山之役，有風從西來入營。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mangshan, a wind came from the west into the camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Mangshan, a wind came from the west into the camp.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「小人風來，當大勝。」

translations.literal: Yexing said: "When a petty man’s wind comes, there will be a great victory."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said, "When a petty man’s wind comes, there will be a great victory."

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「若勝，以爾為本州刺史。」

translations.literal: Shenwu said: "If we win, I shall make you Governor of Benzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "If we win, I shall make you Governor of Benzhou."

sentences.zh: 既而以為太原太守。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was made Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was made Governor of Taiyuan.
