sentences.zh: 五年，齊文襄引為中外府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wenxiang of Qi brought him in as Consulting General of the Inner-and-Outer Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Wenxiang brought him in as Consulting General of the Inner-and-Outer Office.

sentences.zh: 後坐事禁止，業興乃造《九宮行棋曆》，以五百為章，四千四十為蔀，九百八十七為升分，還以己未為元，始終相維，不復移轉，與今曆法術不同。

translations.literal: Later, because of an offense he was confined; Yexing then devised the Nine Palaces Moving-Chess Calendar, taking five hundred as a chapter, four thousand forty as an obscuration, nine hundred eighty-seven as ascending parts, and further taking jiwei as the origin; beginning and end were linked without further shifting, differing from present calendrical methods.
translations.idiomatic: Later, confined for an offense, Yexing devised the Nine Palaces Moving-Chess Calendar, with five hundred as a chapter, four thousand forty as an obscuration, and nine hundred eighty-seven as ascending parts, taking jiwei as the origin with fixed linkage throughout, differing from present calendrical methods.

sentences.zh: 至於氣序交分，景度盈縮，不異也。

translations.literal: As for seasonal qi, equinoxes and solstices, and the waxing and waning of solar measure, there was no difference.
translations.idiomatic: For seasonal qi, equinoxes and solstices, and solar measure, it did not differ.

sentences.zh: 文襄之征潁川，業興曰：「往必克，克後凶。」

translations.literal: When Wenxiang campaigned against Yingchuan, Yexing said: "If you go you will surely conquer; after conquering there will be misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang campaigned against Yingchuan, Yexing said, "If you go you will surely conquer; after conquering there will be misfortune."

sentences.zh: 文襄既克，欲以業興當凶而殺之。

translations.literal: After Wenxiang had conquered, he wished to make Yexing bear the misfortune and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxiang conquered, he wished to make Yexing bear the misfortune and kill him.

sentences.zh: 業興愛好墳籍，鳩集不已。

translations.literal: Yexing loved and collected tomb classics, gathering without end.
translations.idiomatic: He collected books endlessly.

sentences.zh: 手自補修，躬加題帖，其家所有，垂將萬卷。

translations.literal: He personally repaired them and added title slips; his household holdings approached ten thousand chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He collated nearly ten thousand volumes at home.

sentences.zh: 覽讀不息，多有異聞，諸儒服其深博。

translations.literal: Reading without rest, he had many unusual reports; Confucians submitted to his depth and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired his erudition.

sentences.zh: 性豪俠，重意氣，人有急難，委命歸之，便能容匿。

translations.literal: By nature bold and chivalrous, he valued spirit; when men had urgent trouble they entrusted themselves to him and he could shelter them.
translations.idiomatic: He sheltered those in trouble.

sentences.zh: 與其好合，傾身無吝；

translations.literal: With those he favored he gave himself without stint;
translations.idiomatic: He was generous to friends.

sentences.zh: 有乖忤，便即疵毀，乃至聲色，加以謗罵。

translations.literal: With those who crossed him he at once found fault, even raising voices and adding slander.
translations.idiomatic: He fiercely attacked enemies.

sentences.zh: 性又躁隘，至於論難之際，無儒者之風。

translations.literal: He was also rash and narrow; in debates he lacked Confucian bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he lacked scholarly restraint.

sentences.zh: 每語人云：「但道我好，雖知妄言，故勝道惡。」

translations.literal: He often told people: "Just say I am good—even if you know it is false talk, it still beats saying I am bad.
translations.idiomatic: He said false praise beat honest blame.

sentences.zh: 務進忌前，不顧後患，時人以此惡之。

translations.literal: He strove to advance and envied those before him, not caring for later trouble; men of the time hated him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His ambition and jealousy made him widely disliked.

sentences.zh: 至於學術精微，當時莫及。

translations.literal: Yet in the subtlety of scholarship, none of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarly depth none could match him.

sentences.zh: 業興二子，崇祖傳父業。

translations.literal: Yexing had two sons; Chongzu inherited his father's profession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongzu followed his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 崇祖字子述。

translations.literal: Chongzu was styled Zishu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu, courtesy name Zishu.

sentences.zh: 文襄集朝士，命盧景裕講《易》。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang gathered court gentlemen and ordered Lu Jingyu to lecture on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang had Lu Jingyu lecture on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 崇祖時年十一，論難往復，景裕憚之。

translations.literal: Chongzu was then eleven; in debate back and forth Jingyu feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Chongzu debated Lu Jingyu into respect.

sentences.zh: 業興助成其子，至於忿鬩。

translations.literal: Yexing helped his son to success, to the point of angry quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing quarreled helping his son.

sentences.zh: 文襄色甚不平。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang's expression was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was displeased.

sentences.zh: 姚文安難服虔《左傳解》七十七條，名曰《駁妄》。

translations.literal: Yao Wen'an challenged Fu Qian's seventy-seven entries of Zuo commentary explanation, titled Refuting Error.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wen'an wrote Refuting Error against Fu Qian.

sentences.zh: 崇祖申明服氏，名曰《釋謬》。

translations.literal: Chongzu clarified the Fu school, titled Explaining Error.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu wrote Explaining Error in defense.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣營構三台，材瓦工程，皆崇祖所算也。

translations.literal: When Qi Wenxuan built the three towers, timber and tile calculations were all Chongzu's.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu calculated materials for Wenxuan's three towers.

sentences.zh: 封屯留縣侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 遵祖，齊天保初難宗景曆甚精。

translations.literal: Zunzu, in early Tianbao of Qi, was skilled in Zong Jingli's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qi Tianbao Zunzu mastered Zong Jingli's calendar.

sentences.zh: 崇祖為元子武卜葬地，醉而告之曰：「改葬後，當不異孝文。」

translations.literal: Chongzu divined a burial site for Yuanzi Wu while drunk and told him: "After the reburial it will not differ from Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu drunkenly predicted Wu's reburial would match Xiaowen's fortune.

sentences.zh: 武成，或告之，兄弟伏法。

translations.literal: When Wu succeeded, someone reported this; the brothers were executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu became emperor they reported it and both brothers were executed.

sentences.zh: 李鉉，字寶鼎，勃海南皮人也。

translations.literal: Li Xuan, styled Baoding, was a man of Nanpi in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan, courtesy name Baoding, was from Nanpi in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 九歲入學，書《急就篇》，月餘便通。

translations.literal: At nine he entered school and studied the Rapid Writing Primer; in a little over a month he mastered it.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he mastered the Rapid Writing Primer in a month.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，常春夏務農，冬乃入學。

translations.literal: The family was always poor; in spring and summer they worked the fields, and only in winter entered school.
translations.idiomatic: The family farmed in summer and studied in winter.

sentences.zh: 年十六，從浮陽李周仁受《毛詩》、《尚書》，章武劉子猛受《禮記》，常山房虯受《周官》、《儀禮》，漁陽鮮于靈馥受《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: At sixteen he received the Mao Odes and Documents from Li Zhouren of Fuyang, the Rites from Liu Zimeng of Zhangwu, the Offices of Zhou and Ceremonial Rites from Fang Qiu of Changshan, and the Zuo Spring and Autumn from Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he studied under several masters in the region.

sentences.zh: 鉉以鄉里無可師者，遂與州裏楊元懿、河間宗惠振等結友，詣大儒徐遵明受業。

translations.literal: Because locally there were no teachers worth having, he with Yang Yuanyi of the province and Zong Huizhen of Hejian and others became friends and went to the great Confucian Xu Zunming for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Xu Zunming when local teachers were insufficient.

sentences.zh: 居徐門下五年，常稱高第。

translations.literal: He dwelt at Xu's gate five years and was always called a high-grade student.
translations.idiomatic: He studied five years at Xu's gate as a top student.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，便自潛居討論是非。

translations.literal: At twenty-three he secluded himself to discuss right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three he withdrew to debate doctrine.

sentences.zh: 撰定《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《三禮義疏》及《三傳異同》、《周易義例》合三十餘卷。

translations.literal: He composed commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, Meaning and Commentary of the Three Rites, Differences of the Three Commentaries, and Examples of the Changes' Meaning—over thirty chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote over thirty chapters of commentary on the classics.

sentences.zh: 用心精苦，曾三秋冬不畜枕，每睡，假寐而已。

translations.literal: His effort was bitterly exacting; for three autumns and winters he kept no pillow, sleeping only in brief naps.
translations.idiomatic: He often slept without a pillow, napping briefly.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，歸養二親，因教授鄉里。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he returned to nourish both parents and taught in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he returned home to care for his parents and teach.

sentences.zh: 生徒恆數百人，燕趙間能言經者，多出其門。

translations.literal: Disciples constantly numbered several hundred; among Yan and Zhao those who could discourse on the classics mostly came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds studied with him; many Yan-Zhao classicists were his students.

sentences.zh: 以鄉里寡文籍，來游京師，讀所未見書。

translations.literal: Because his district lacked literary collections, he came to the capital to read books he had not seen.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the capital to read rare books.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除太學博士。

translations.literal: At that time the Directorate had few staff; he was summoned as Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as National University erudite.

sentences.zh: 及李同軌卒，齊神武令文襄在京妙簡碩學，以教諸子。

translations.literal: He was also made Concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He also became Concurrent Cavalier Attendant and Libationer.

sentences.zh: 文襄以鉉應旨，徵詣晉陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen ordered the princes to choose masters; Xuan was appointed master to the Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen had princes choose masters; Xuan taught the Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 時中山石曜、北平陽絢、北海王晞、清河崔瞻、廣平宋欽道及工書人韓毅同在東館，師友諸王。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to the Imperial Clan as teacher to the Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He later taught the Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 鉉以去聖久遠，文字多有乖謬，於講授之暇，遂覽《說文》、《倉》、《雅》，刪正六藝經注中謬字，名曰《字辨》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang he was made Concurrent Palace Attendant and Libationer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhengguang he was palace attendant and libationer.

sentences.zh: 天保初，詔鉉與殿中尚書邢邵，中書令魏收等參議禮律，仍兼國子博士。

translations.literal: He was ordered to lecture on the Rites and Documents in the Chongxun Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on Rites and Documents in the Chongxun Hall.

sentences.zh: 時詔北平太守宋景業、西河太守綦母懷文等草定新曆，錄尚書、平原王高隆之令鉉與通直常侍房延祐、國子博士刁柔參考得失。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 尋正國子博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu performed the libation ceremony, he was made Concurrent Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's libation ceremony he became Concurrent Minister.

sentences.zh: 廢帝之在東宮，文宣詔鉉以經入授，甚見優禮。

translations.literal: He was also made Grand Tutor to the Prince of Qinghe and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand Tutor to the Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 卒，特贈廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiaochang year three.

sentences.zh: 及還葬，王人將送，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Minister of Works and Governor of Yanzhou with posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Minister of Works and Governor of Yanzhou, titled Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 楊元懿、宗惠振官俱至國子博士。

translations.literal: His son Shaozu inherited the title and also had talent for the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaozu inherited the title and mastered classics.

sentences.zh: 馮偉，字偉節，中山字喜人也。

translations.literal: Feng Wei, styled Zikai, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Wei, courtesy name Zikai, was from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，衣冠甚偉，見者肅然。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Xu Zunming and was skilled in the Mao Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Xu Zunming in the Mao Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 少從李寶鼎學，李重其聰敏，恆別意試問之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he was made doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year three he was National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 多所通解，尤明《禮》、《傳》。

translations.literal: He was also made Libationer and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Libationer and died in office.

sentences.zh: 後還鄉里，閉門不出，將三十年。

translations.literal: Zhang Mainu, styled Zhujie, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mainu, courtesy name Zhujie, was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 不問生產，不交賓客，專精覃思，無所不通。

translations.literal: His family name was originally Du; because of his father's crime he was castrated and became a eunuch, hence the Zhang surname.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was Du; castration made him a eunuch surnamed Zhang.

sentences.zh: 齊趙郡王出鎮定州，以禮迎接，命書三至，縣令親至其門，猶辭疾不起。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the Rites and Zuo Tradition and constantly received instruction from Xu Zunming.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Rites and the Zuo under Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 王將命駕致請，佐吏前後星馳報之，縣令又自為其整冠履，不得已而出。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved south, Mainu with Xiong Ansheng and others followed the campaign as masters of the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiaowen's southern campaign as a ritual master.

sentences.zh: 王下査事迎之，止其拜伏，分階而上，留之賓館，甚見禮重。

translations.literal: He was made Libationer of the National University and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Libationer and died in office.

sentences.zh: 王將舉充秀才，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Liu Guisi, styled Zhengli, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guisi, courtesy name Zhengli, was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 歲餘請還。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Xu Zunming and was skilled in the Mao Odes and Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Mao Odes and Zuo under Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 王知其不願拘束，以禮發遣，贈遺甚厚。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in ritual and music and was famed in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was also famed in Ji for ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 一無所納，唯受時服而已。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he was made doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year three he was National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 及還，不交人事，郡守縣令，每親至。

translations.literal: He was also made Libationer and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Libationer and died in office.

sentences.zh: 歲時或置羊酒，亦辭不納。

translations.literal: Guisi's conduct was pure and he did not seek advancement; he was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure and unambitious, praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 門徒束脩，一毫不受。

translations.literal: Bao Jixiang, styled Yanhe, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jixiang, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 蠶而衣，耕而飯，簞食瓢飲，不改其樂。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Xu Zunming and was skilled in the Mao Odes and Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Mao Odes and Zuo under Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 以壽終。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he was made doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year three he was National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 張買奴，平原人也。

translations.literal: He was also made Libationer and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Libationer and died in office.

sentences.zh: 經義該博，門徒千餘人，諸儒咸推重之。

translations.literal: Xing Zhi, styled Zijing, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zhi, courtesy name Zijing, was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，曆太學博士、國子助教，卒。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Xu Zunming and was skilled in the Mao Odes and Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Mao Odes and Zuo under Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 劉軌思，勃海人也。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in the Rites and was famed in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was also famed in Ji for the Rites.

sentences.zh: 說《詩》甚精。

translations.literal: He lectured on the Odes with great precision.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on the Odes with great precision.

sentences.zh: 少事同郡劉敬和，敬和事同郡程師則，故其鄉曲多為《詩》者。

translations.literal: In youth he served Liu Jinghe of the same commandery; Jinghe served Cheng Shize of the same commandery—thus in his home district many studied the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: His local tradition of Odes study ran through Liu Jinghe and Cheng Shize.

sentences.zh: 軌思仕齊，位國子博士。

translations.literal: Guisi served Qi and reached National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Guisi served Qi as National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 鮑季詳，勃海人也。

translations.literal: Bao Jixiang was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jixiang was from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 甚明《禮》，兼通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He was very clear in the Rites and also penetrated the Zuo Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert in Rites and the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 少時，恆為李寶鼎都講。

translations.literal: In youth he was always chief lecturer for Li Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was chief lecturer for Li Xuan.

sentences.zh: 後亦自有徒眾，諸儒稱之。

translations.literal: Later he also had his own following; Confucians praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He later had his own school and was praised.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，卒于太學博士。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he died as National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he died as National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 從弟長暄，兼通《禮》、《傳》。

translations.literal: His younger cousin cousin Changxuan was also versed in the Rites and Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Changxuan also mastered Rites and the Tradition.

sentences.zh: 為任城王湝丞相掾。

translations.literal: He was aide to the Prince of Rencheng, Wang Ti.
translations.idiomatic: He was aide to Prince Ti of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 恆在都教授貴游子弟。

translations.literal: He constantly taught noble youths in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He taught noble youths in the capital.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，卒於家。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he died at home.

sentences.zh: 邢峙，字士峻，河間鄭人也。

translations.literal: Xing Zhi, styled Shijun, was a man of Zheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zhi, courtesy name Shijun, was from Zheng in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少學通《三禮》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: From youth his learning penetrated the Three Rites and Zuo Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he mastered the Three Rites and Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，初為四門博士，遷國子助教，以經入授皇太子。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he was first Four Gates doctor, then National University assistant teacher, entering to teach the crown prince the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he taught the crown prince after rising from Four Gates doctor.

sentences.zh: 峙方正純厚，有儒者風。

translations.literal: Zhi was upright, pure, and thick, with the air of a Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was upright and had a scholar's bearing.

sentences.zh: 廚宰進太子食，菜有邪蒿，峙令去之，曰：「此菜有不正之名，非殿下宜食。」

translations.literal: When the kitchen presented the crown prince's food with wormwood in the greens, Zhi ordered it removed, saying: "This vegetable has an inauspicious name—not fit for the heir to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He removed wormwood from the crown prince's meal as inauspiciously named.

sentences.zh: 文宣聞而嘉之，賜以被褥縑纊，拜國子博士。

translations.literal: Wen Xuan heard and praised this, bestowing quilts and silk, and made him National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xuan praised him and made him National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，除清河太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was made governor of Qinghe with benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangjian's start he governed Qinghe benevolently.

sentences.zh: 年老歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Old, he returned home and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 劉晝，字孔昭，勃海阜城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhou, styled Kongzhao, was a man of Fucheng in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhou, courtesy name Kongzhao, was from Fucheng in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，愛學，伏膺無倦。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he loved learning and received instruction without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he studied tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 常閉戶讀書，暑月唯著犢鼻褌。

translations.literal: He constantly shut his door to read; in summer he wore only calf-nose breeches.
translations.idiomatic: He read behind closed doors, wearing only summer breeches.

sentences.zh: 與儒者李寶鼎同鄉，甚相親愛。

translations.literal: He was very close with the Confucian Li Baoding of his district.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Li Baoding of his district.

sentences.zh: 寶鼎授其《三禮》，又就馬敬德習《服氏春秋》，俱通大義。

translations.literal: Baoding taught him the Three Rites; he also studied Fu Qian's Spring and Autumn under Ma Jingde, both penetrating great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan and Ma Jingde taught him Rites and the Zuo.

sentences.zh: 恨下里少墳籍，便杖策入都。

translations.literal: Regretting few tomb classics in his district, he went to the capital with staff in hand.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital seeking books.

sentences.zh: 知鄴令宋世良家有書五千卷，乃求為其子博士，恣意披覽，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Knowing Magistrate Song Shiliang of Ye had five thousand volumes, he sought to be his son's teacher and read freely day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: He read Song Shiliang's five thousand volumes day and night.

sentences.zh: 還，舉秀才，策不第，乃恨不學屬文，方復緝綴辭藻。

translations.literal: Returning, he was recommended as provincial talent but failed the examination; he regretted not studying literary composition and again wove phrases.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the talent exam and turned to writing.

sentences.zh: 言甚古掘，制一首賦，以六合為名，自謂絕倫，乃歎儒者勞而寡功。

translations.literal: His words were very archaic; composing one fu named "Six Harmonies," he deemed it peerless and sighed that Confucians labor with little result.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an arrogant fu called "Six Harmonies."

sentences.zh: 曾以賦呈魏收而不拜。

translations.literal: He once presented the fu to Wei Shou without bowing.
translations.idiomatic: He presented it to Wei Shou without courtesy.

sentences.zh: 收忿之，謂曰：「賦名六合，已是太愚，文又愚於六合。

translations.literal: Shou was angry and said: "The fu's title Six Harmonies is already too foolish, and the text is more foolish than Six Harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou angrily said, "The title Six Harmonies is already too foolish, and the text is more foolish than Six Harmonies.

sentences.zh: 君四體又甘於文。」

translations.literal: Your four limbs are sweeter than the text."
translations.idiomatic: Your limbs are sweeter than the text."

sentences.zh: 晝不忿，又以示邢子才。

translations.literal: Zhou was displeased and showed it to Xing Zicai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, displeased, showed it to Xing Zicai.

sentences.zh: 子才曰：「君此賦，正似疥駱駝，伏而無嫵媚。」

translations.literal: Zicai said: "Your fu is just like a scabby camel lying down without charm."
translations.idiomatic: Zicai said it was like a scabby camel lying down without charm.

sentences.zh: 晝求秀才，十年不得，發憤撰《高才不遇傳》。

translations.literal: Zhou sought to be provincial talent but for ten years did not obtain it; in anger he composed Biographies of Talents Who Met No Success.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years of failing to become provincial talent, he wrote Biographies of Unsuccessful Talents.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史酈伯偉見之，始舉晝，時年四十八。

translations.literal: Governor Li Bawei of Ji saw it and first recommended Zhou at age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bawei recommended him at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 刺史隴西李璵，亦嘗以晝應詔。

translations.literal: Governor Li Yu of Longxi also once recommended Zhou in response to an imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Yu of Longxi also once recommended Zhou in response to an imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 先告之，晝曰：「公自為國舉才，何勞語晝！」

translations.literal: He informed Zhou beforehand; Zhou said: "You yourself recommend talent for the state—why trouble Zhou with word of it!"
translations.idiomatic: He informed Zhou beforehand; Zhou said, "You yourself recommend talent for the state—why bother telling me!"

sentences.zh: 齊河南王孝瑜聞晝名，每召見，輒與促席對飲。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaoyu of Henan of Qi heard Zhou’s fame; whenever he summoned him, they would sit close and drink together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaoyu of Henan heard of Zhou and, whenever he summoned him, would sit close and drink with him.

sentences.zh: 後遇有密親，使且在齋坐，晝須臾徑去，追謝要之，終不復屈。

translations.literal: Later when he had a private relative present, he had Zhou wait in the study; Zhou shortly left straight away. Pursued and entreated to stay, he never yielded again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when a private relative was present, he had Zhou wait in the study; Zhou soon left. Though pursued and entreated to stay, he never yielded again.

sentences.zh: 孝昭即位，好受直言。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao ascended, he loved to receive blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao ascended, he welcomed blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 晝聞之，喜曰：「董仲舒、公孫弘可以出矣。」

translations.literal: Zhou heard this and said with joy: "Dong Zhongshu and Gongsun Hong may now come forth!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou heard this and said joyfully, "Dong Zhongshu and Gongsun Hong may now come forth!"

sentences.zh: 乃步詣晉陽上書，言亦切直，而多非世要，終不見收采。

translations.literal: He then walked to Jinyang and submitted a memorial; his words were also blunt and direct, but much was not what the age required, and in the end he was not accepted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He walked to Jinyang and submitted a memorial; though blunt and direct, much of it missed what the age required, and he was never employed.

sentences.zh: 編錄所上之書，為《帝道》。

translations.literal: He compiled and recorded the book he submitted as The Imperial Way.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled his submitted writings as The Imperial Way.

sentences.zh: 河清中，又著《金箱璧言》，蓋以指機政之不良。

translations.literal: During Heqing he also wrote Golden Casket and Jade Words, intending thereby to point to the defects of confidential government.
translations.idiomatic: During Heqing he also wrote Golden Casket and Jade Words, evidently to criticize defects in confidential government.

sentences.zh: 晝夜嘗夢貴人若吏部尚書者補交州興俊令，寤而密書記之。

translations.literal: Zhou once dreamed a noble like Minister of Personnel appointed him Magistrate of Xingjun in Jiaozhou; waking, he secretly recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of appointment as magistrate of Xingjun and recorded it on waking.

sentences.zh: 卒後旬餘，其家幼女鬼語，聲似晝，云「我被用為興俊縣令，得假暫來辭別」云。

translations.literal: A little over ten days after his death, his household's young daughter spoke with a ghost's voice like Zhou, saying: "I was used as Magistrate of Xingjun and have leave to come bid farewell."
translations.idiomatic: After death his daughter seemed possessed by his voice, saying he had been appointed magistrate of Xingjun.

sentences.zh: 晝常自謂博物奇才，言好矜大。

translations.literal: Zhou often considered himself a museum talent of rare learning and spoke with fond boasting.
translations.idiomatic: He often boasted of his erudition.

sentences.zh: 每言：「使我數十卷書行於後世，不易齊景之千駟也。」

translations.literal: He often said: "Let several tens of my chapters circulate in later ages—it is no harder than Duke Jing of Qi's thousand teams of horses."
translations.idiomatic: He said his books would outshine mere wealth.

sentences.zh: 容止舒緩，舉動不倫，由是竟無仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: His bearing was slow and his conduct unlike others; because of this he never obtained office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: His odd manner kept him from office; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 馬敬德，河間人也。

translations.literal: Ma Jingde was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jingde was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少好儒術，負笈隨徐遵明學《詩》、《禮》，略通大義，而不能精。

translations.literal: From youth he loved Confucian arts, bore a satchel and followed Xu Zunming in the Odes and Rites, roughly penetrating great meaning but not refining it.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Odes and Rites under Xu Zunming without full mastery.

sentences.zh: 遂留意于《春秋左氏》，沈思研求，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: He then focused on the Zuo Spring and Autumn, pondering and seeking deeply day and night without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He then devoted himself to the Zuo Commentary day and night.

sentences.zh: 教授于燕、趙間，生徒隨之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Teaching between Yan and Zhao, followers were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He taught widely in Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 乃詣州將，求秀才。

translations.literal: He then went to the provincial governor seeking recommendation as provincial talent.
translations.idiomatic: He sought recommendation as provincial talent.

sentences.zh: 將以其純儒，無意推薦。

translations.literal: The governor, because he was a pure Confucian, had no intent to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: The governor hesitated to recommend a bookish man.

sentences.zh: 敬德請試方略，五條皆有文理，乃欣然舉送。

translations.literal: Jingde requested trial in strategy and tactics; five questions all had pattern and reason, and the governor gladly sent him up.
translations.idiomatic: He passed a strategy exam and was recommended.

sentences.zh: 至都，唯得中第。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital he only ranked middle in the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he ranked only middle tier.

sentences.zh: 請試經業，問十條，並通。

translations.literal: He requested trial in classical studies; of ten questions he passed all.
translations.idiomatic: He passed ten classical questions.

sentences.zh: 擢授國子助教，再遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted National University assistant teacher and again moved to National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made National University assistant teacher, then promoted again to National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 齊武成為後主擇師傅，趙彥深進之，入為侍講。

translations.literal: When Qi Wucheng chose a tutor for the Later Lord, Zhao Yanshen recommended Jingde, who entered as lecturer-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng chose the heir's tutor, Zhao Yanshen recommended Ma Jingde as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 其妻夜夢猛獸將來向之，敬德走超叢棘，妻伏地不敢動。

translations.literal: His wife dreamed at night that a fierce beast was coming toward her; Jingde ran leaping over thorn thickets while his wife lay prostrate and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: His wife dreamed of a beast; he leapt thorn bushes in the dream.

sentences.zh: 敬德占曰：「吾當為大官。

translations.literal: Jingde divined and said: "I shall become a great officer.
translations.idiomatic: He divined: "I shall become a great officer.

sentences.zh: 超棘，過幾卿也；

translations.literal: Leaping thorn thickets means passing several ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Leaping thickets means rising through ranks;

sentences.zh: 爾伏地，夫人也。」

translations.literal: your lying prostrate means the lady.
translations.idiomatic: your prostration means my wife.

sentences.zh: 後主既不好學，敬德侍講甚疏，時時以《春秋》入授。

translations.literal: The Later Lord did not love learning; Jingde's lecturing was very sparse, yet from time to time he entered to teach the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The heir disliked study; Jingde taught him the Spring and Autumn sparingly.

sentences.zh: 猶以師傅恩，拜國子祭酒、儀同三司、金紫光祿大夫、瀛州大中正。

translations.literal: Still, because of his merit as tutor, he was made Libationer of the National University, Equal to the Third Rank, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal, and Grand Rectifier of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Libationer and high minister for his service as tutor.

sentences.zh: 卒，其徒曰：「馬生勝孔子，孔子不得儀同。」

translations.literal: When he died his disciples said: "Master Ma surpasses Confucius—Confucius did not obtain Equal to the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His students joked he outranked Confucius.

sentences.zh: 尋贈開府、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Grand Guardian and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後，侍書張景仁封王，趙彥深云：「何容侍書封王，侍講翻無封爵？」

translations.literal: Later, Attendant Scribe Zhang Jingren was enfeoffed as king; Zhao Yanshen said: "How can an attendant scribe be king while the lecturer has no fief?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen protested that the lecturer lacked a fief when the scribe became king.

sentences.zh: 亦追封敬德廣漢郡王，令子元熙襲。

translations.literal: Jingde was also posthumously enfeoffed King of Guanghan commandery, with his son Yuanxi to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde was posthumously made King of Guanghan; his son Yuanxi inherited.

sentences.zh: 元熙字長明，少傳父業，兼長文藻。

translations.literal: Yuanxi, styled Changming, from youth inherited his father's profession and was also skilled in literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi inherited his father's learning and excelled in letters.

sentences.zh: 以通直待詔文林館。

translations.literal: He served as Regular Attendant awaiting orders at the Wulin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served at the Wulin Hall.

sentences.zh: 武平中，皇太子將講《孝經》，有司請擇師。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era, when the crown prince was about to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, the offices requested choosing a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince studied the Filial Piety classic, a teacher was sought.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「馬元熙，朕師之子，文學不惡。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ma Yuanxi is my teacher's son; his letters are not bad.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor chose Ma Yuanxi, the lecturer's son.

sentences.zh: 於是以《孝經》入授皇太子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered to teach the crown prince the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the crown prince the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 儒者榮其世載。

translations.literal: Confucians honored this succession through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honored the family's continuity.

sentences.zh: 性和厚，在內甚得名譽。

translations.literal: His nature was harmonious and thick; within the palace he gained great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and respected at court.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于秦王文學。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as literary attendant to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he died as literary attendant to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 張景仁，濟北人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingren was a man of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingren was from Jibei.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，家貧，以學書為業，遂工草隸。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, the family poor, he took learning calligraphy as his profession and became skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he mastered calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 選補內書生，與魏郡姚元標、潁川韓毅、同郡袁買奴、滎陽李超等齊名，文襄並引為賓客。

translations.literal: Selected as inner academy student, he with Yao Yuanbiao of Wei commandery, Han Yi of Yingchuan, Yuan Mainu of the same commandery, and Li Chao of Xingyang were equally famous; Wen Xiang all drew them as guests.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed among inner academy calligraphers under Wen Xiang.

sentences.zh: 天保八年，敕教太原王紹德書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao an edict ordered him teach Prince Shaode of Taiyuan calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year eight he taught the Prince of Taiyuan calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，武成令侍書，遂被引擢。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace, Wucheng ordered him attendant scribe and he was drawn up in promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng made him attendant scribe to the heir.

sentences.zh: 小心恭謹，後主愛之，呼為博士。

translations.literal: Careful and respectful, the Later Lord loved him and called him Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: The heir called him Doctor.

sentences.zh: 登祚，累遷通直散騎常侍，在左右。

translations.literal: On succeeding to the throne he was repeatedly moved to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Regular Attendant at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 與語，猶稱博士。

translations.literal: In conversation he still called him Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still called him Doctor in conversation.

sentences.zh: 胡人何洪珍有寵於後主，欲得通婚朝士。

translations.literal: The barbarian He Hongzhen was favored by the Later Lord and wished to marry with court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongzhen sought marriage ties with courtiers.

sentences.zh: 以景仁在內，官位稍高，遂為其兄子取景仁第二息瑜之女，因以表裹相援，恩遇日隆。

translations.literal: Because Jingren was within the palace with somewhat high rank, he took Jingren's second son Yu's daughter for his brother's son, and through inner and outer support favor grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: He married Jingren's granddaughter and grew powerful through the connection.

sentences.zh: 景仁多疾，帝每遣徐之範等療之，給藥物珍羞，中使問疾，相望於道。

translations.literal: Jingren had many illnesses; the emperor often sent Xu Zhifan and others to treat him, giving drugs and delicacies; palace envoys inquiring after his illness filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor constantly sent physicians and gifts.

sentences.zh: 是後，敕有司恆就宅送禦食。

translations.literal: After this an edict ordered the offices always to send imperial food to his house.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial food was sent to his home daily.

sentences.zh: 車駕或有行幸，在道宿處，每送步障，為遮風寒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled, at lodging places on the road they always sent screens to ward off wind and cold.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial journeys screens were sent to protect him.

sentences.zh: 進位儀同三司，加開府，侍書如故。

translations.literal: He advanced to Equal to the Third Rank, was additionally made Grand Guardian, and attendant scribe as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Equal to the Third Rank and Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 每旦須參，即在東宮停止。

translations.literal: Each morning he had to attend and stopped at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He attended daily and lodged at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 及立文林館，中人鄧長顒希旨，奏令總判館事。

translations.literal: When the Wulin Hall was established, the inner attendant Deng Changyuan to please the emperor memorialized that Jingren should oversee the hall's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Changyuan had him oversee the Wulin Hall.

sentences.zh: 除侍中，封建安王。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 洪珍死後，長顒猶存舊款，更相彌縫，得無墜退。

translations.literal: After Hongzhen's death Changyuan still kept the old tie; they supported each other so he did not fall back.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzhen died he kept influence through Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 遂除中書監，卒。

translations.literal: He was then made Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became Secretariat Director and died.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、五州刺史、司空公。

translations.literal: Posthumously Attendant-in-Ordinary, Governor of the Five Provinces, and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously high minister and Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 景仁為兒童時，在洛京，曾詣國學摹《石經》。

translations.literal: When Jingren was a child in Luoyang he once went to the National University to copy the Stone Classics.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy in Luoyang he copied the Stone Classics at the National University.

sentences.zh: 許子華遇之學中，執景仁手曰：「張郎風骨，必當通貴，非但官爵遷達，乃與天子同筆硯，傳衣履。」

translations.literal: Xu Zihua met him in the academy, took Jingren's hand and said: "Master Zhang's bearing will surely reach high nobility—not only offices and ranks, but sharing brush and ink with the Son of Heaven, transmitting robe and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zihua predicted he would share the emperor's writing tools.

sentences.zh: 子華卒二十餘年，景仁位開府，數賜衣冠、筆硯，如子華所言。

translations.literal: Over twenty years after Zihua's death, Jingren reached Grand Guardian; several times he was bestowed robes, brush, and ink—as Zihua had said.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua's prediction came true.

sentences.zh: 出自寒微，本無識見，一旦開府、侍中、封王。

translations.literal: Coming from cold baseness, originally without insight, suddenly Grand Guardian, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and enfeoffed king.
translations.idiomatic: From humble origins he rose to king and attendant.

sentences.zh: 其婦姓奇，莫知氏族所出，容制音辭，事事庸俚。

translations.literal: His wife's surname was Qi; no one knew what clan she came from; her appearance, speech, and voice were vulgar in everything.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was of obscure and vulgar background.

sentences.zh: 既除王妃，與諸公主、郡君，同在朝謁之列，見者為其慚悚。

translations.literal: Once made princess consort, with the various princesses and commandery ladies she stood in the same court audience—viewers were ashamed for her.
translations.idiomatic: As princess consort she embarrassed court audiences.

sentences.zh: 景仁性本卑謙，及用胡人、巷伯之勢，坐致通顯，志操頗改，漸成驕傲。

translations.literal: Jingren's nature was originally humble, but using barbarian and alley eunuch power he sat and reached manifest eminence; his will and conduct quite changed and gradually became arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Success through eunuch patronage made him arrogant.

sentences.zh: 良馬輕裘，徒從擁冗；

translations.literal: Fine horses and light fur coats; attendants crowded in numbers;
translations.idiomatic: He lived ostentatiously with fine horses and many attendants.

sentences.zh: 高門廣宇，當衢向術。

translations.literal: High gates and broad houses facing the main thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: He built grand houses on main streets.

sentences.zh: 諸子不思其本，自許貴遊。

translations.literal: His sons did not think of their origins and deemed themselves noble wanderers.
translations.idiomatic: His sons acted like spoiled nobles.

sentences.zh: 自倉頡以來，八體取進，一人而已。

translations.literal: From Cang Jie onward, of the eight script forms only one man advanced by them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Cang Jie only one man had risen through the eight scripts.

sentences.zh: 權會，字正理，河間鄭人也。

translations.literal: Quan Hui, styled Zhengli, was a man of Zheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Hui, courtesy name Zhengli, was from Zheng in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 志尚沈雅，動遵禮則。

translations.literal: His will and esteem were deep and elegant; in movement he followed ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was refined and observant of ritual.

sentences.zh: 少受鄭《易》，妙盡幽微；

translations.literal: In youth he received Zheng's Changes and wonderfully exhausted its subtle depths;
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Zheng's Changes.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《書》、《二禮》，文義該洽；

translations.literal: in the Odes, Documents, and Two Rites his literary meaning was comprehensive;
translations.idiomatic: He was comprehensive in Odes, Documents, and Two Rites.

sentences.zh: 兼明風角，妙識玄象。

translations.literal: he was also clear in wind angles and wonderfully knew dark signs.
translations.idiomatic: He knew wind divination and astrology.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，初四門博士。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he was first Four Gates doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he was first Four Gates doctor.

sentences.zh: 僕射崔暹引為館客，甚敬重焉，命世子達挐盡師傅之禮。

translations.literal: Vice Director Cui Xian drew him as lodge guest and greatly respected him, ordering the heir apparent Da to perform full tutor's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian honored him and had the heir treat him as tutor.

sentences.zh: 暹欲薦會與馬敬德等為諸王師。

translations.literal: Xian wished to recommend Hui with Ma Jingde and others as tutors to the various princes.
translations.idiomatic: Xian wished to make him a prince's tutor.

sentences.zh: 會性恬靜，不慕榮勢，恥于左宦，固辭。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was quiet and still; he did not admire glory and power, and was ashamed of left-hand offices—he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hui declined office from modesty.

sentences.zh: 暹識其意，遂罷薦舉。

translations.literal: Xian knew his intent and therefore stopped the recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Xian accepted his refusal.

sentences.zh: 尋追修國史，監知太史局事。

translations.literal: Soon he pursued editing the national history and supervised the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He edited national history and supervised astronomy.

sentences.zh: 後遷國子博士。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He later became National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 會參掌雖繁，教授不闕。

translations.literal: Though Hui's concurrent duties were numerous, teaching was not neglected.
translations.idiomatic: He never neglected teaching despite many duties.

sentences.zh: 性甚儒綍，似不能言，及臨機答難，酬報如響，由是為諸儒所推。

translations.literal: His nature was very slow and yielding, seeming unable to speak; yet facing sudden questions his answers rang like echoes—therefore Confucians pushed him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Seemingly slow, he answered debates brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 而貴遊子弟慕其德義者，或就其宅，或寄宿鄰家，晝夜承間，受其學業。

translations.literal: Noble wanderers' sons who admired his virtue and righteousness came to his house or lodged with neighbors, day and night availing themselves of intervals to receive his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Noble youths flocked to study with him.

sentences.zh: 會欣然演說，未嘗懈怠。

translations.literal: Hui gladly lectured and never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 雖明風角玄象，至於私室，都不及言。

translations.literal: Though clear in wind angles and dark signs, in private rooms he never spoke of them.
translations.idiomatic: He never discussed divination in private.

sentences.zh: 學徒有請問者，終無所說。

translations.literal: When disciples asked, in the end he said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to teach divination to students.

sentences.zh: 每云：「此學可知不可言，諸君並貴遊子弟，不由此進，何煩問也。」

translations.literal: He often said: "This learning can be known but not spoken; you are all noble wanderers' sons—not advancing by this, why trouble to ask?
translations.idiomatic: He said nobles need not learn divination for advancement.

sentences.zh: 唯有一子，亦不授此術。

translations.literal: He had only one son and did not transmit this art to him either.
translations.idiomatic: He taught divination to no one, not even his son.

sentences.zh: 會曾遣家人遠行，久而不反。

translations.literal: Hui once sent a household member on a distant journey who long did not return.
translations.idiomatic: A servant he sent away was long absent.

sentences.zh: 其行還將至，乃逢寒雪，寄息他舍。

translations.literal: The journey was about to return when they met cold snow and lodged at another house.
translations.idiomatic: The servant was returning through snow.

sentences.zh: 會方處學堂講說，忽有旋風吹雪入戶，會笑曰：「行人至，何意中停！」

translations.literal: Hui was just in the academy lecturing when suddenly a whirlwind blew snow into the door; Hui laughed: "The traveler has come—why stop midway!
translations.idiomatic: During a lecture a whirlwind brought snow; he said the traveler was near.

sentences.zh: 遂使追尋，果如其語。

translations.literal: He sent men to seek and it was indeed as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Seekers found the servant as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 會每占筮，大小必中。

translations.literal: Whenever Hui divined by milfoil, great or small he always hit.
translations.idiomatic: His yarrow divinations always proved right.

sentences.zh: 但用爻辭彖象，以辨吉凶。

translations.literal: He only used line texts and judgment images to distinguish fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He used only classical line texts, not oral formulas.

sentences.zh: 《易》占之屬，都不經口。

translations.literal: Changes divination sorts he never spoke from memory.
translations.idiomatic: He never recited oral divination lore.

sentences.zh: 會本貧生，無僮僕，初任助教日，恆乘驢。

translations.literal: Hui was originally a poor student without servants; in his first days as assistant teacher he always rode a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he rode a donkey as assistant teacher.

sentences.zh: 其職事處多，非晚不歸。

translations.literal: His duties were many and he did not return until late.
translations.idiomatic: He returned late from many duties.

sentences.zh: 曾夜出城東門，會獨乘一驢。

translations.literal: Once at night he went out the eastern gate; Hui rode a donkey alone.
translations.idiomatic: One night he rode out the east gate alone.

sentences.zh: 忽有二人，一人牽頭，一人隨後，有似相助。

translations.literal: Suddenly two men—one leading the head, one following behind—seemed to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Two strange men seemed to escort his donkey.

sentences.zh: 其回動輕漂，有異生人。

translations.literal: Their turning and movement were light and drifting, unlike living men.
translations.idiomatic: They moved oddly, unlike living men.

sentences.zh: 漸失路，不由本道。

translations.literal: Gradually they lost the way and did not follow the proper road.
translations.idiomatic: They left the proper road.

sentences.zh: 心甚怪之，遂誦《易經》上篇第一卷。

translations.literal: His heart greatly wondered at it; he then recited the first chapter of the upper canon of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He recited the Changes to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 不盡，前後二人，忽然離散。

translations.literal: Before finishing, the two before and behind suddenly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the figures vanished.

sentences.zh: 會亦不覺墮驢，迷悶，至明始覺。

translations.literal: Hui also did not know he had fallen from the donkey, dazed until dawn he awoke.
translations.idiomatic: He fell unconscious and awoke at dawn.

sentences.zh: 方知墮處乃是郭外，才去家數里。

translations.literal: Then he knew the fall was outside the city wall, only several li from home.
translations.idiomatic: He had fallen outside the walls near home.

sentences.zh: 有一子，字子襲，聰敏精勤，幼有成人之量。

translations.literal: He had one son, styled Zixi, clever, keen, and diligent, with the measure of an adult from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixi was precocious.

sentences.zh: 先亡。

translations.literal: He died first.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi died first.

sentences.zh: 臨送者為其傷慟，會唯一哭而罷，時人尚其達命。

translations.literal: Those seeing him off grieved for him; Hui cried only once and stopped—men of the time admired his understanding of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Hui mourned briefly, admired for accepting fate.

sentences.zh: 武平末，自府還第，在路無故馬倒，遂不得語，因暴亡。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping, returning from his office to his house, on the road his horse for no reason collapsed; he could not speak and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuping's end his horse fell and he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 注《易》一部，行於世。

translations.literal: His commentary on the Changes in one work circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary on the Changes circulated.

sentences.zh: 會生平畏馬，位望既至，不得不乘，果以此終。

translations.literal: Hui through life feared horses; when rank and gaze had arrived he could not avoid riding—and indeed ended thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He had feared horses yet died after riding when eminent.

sentences.zh: 張思伯，河間樂城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sibo was a man of Lecheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sibo was from Lecheng in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 善說《左氏傳》，為馬敬德之次。

translations.literal: He was skilled at expounding the Zuo Tradition and was second to Ma Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He expounded the Zuo, second only to Ma Jingde.

sentences.zh: 撰《刊例》十卷，行于時。

translations.literal: He composed Editorial Examples in ten chapters circulating at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Editorial Examples in ten chapters.

sentences.zh: 亦為《毛詩》章句。

translations.literal: He also made chapter-and-verse for the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Mao Odes chapter-and-verse.

sentences.zh: 以二經教授齊安王廓。

translations.literal: With the two classics he taught Prince Kuo of Qi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He taught Prince Kuo of Qi'an both classics.

sentences.zh: 位國子博士。

translations.literal: He reached National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He became National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 又有長樂張奉禮，善《三傳》，與思伯齊名。

translations.literal: There was also Zhang Fengli of Chang le, skilled in the Three Commentaries, equally famous with Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengli of Changle was equally famed for the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 位國子助教。

translations.literal: He reached National University assistant teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He became National University assistant teacher.

sentences.zh: 張雕武，中山北平人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Diaowu was a man of Beiping in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Diaowu was from Beiping in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微。

translations.literal: His family for generations was poor and humble.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and humble.

sentences.zh: 其兄蘭武，仕尚書令史，微有資產。

translations.literal: His elder brother Lanwu served as Clerk of the Secretariat Director and had modest property.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Lanwu was a Secretariat clerk with modest means.

sentences.zh: 故護軍長史王元則時為書生，停其宅。

translations.literal: The former Chief Clerk of the Protector-General Wang Yuanze was then a student and lodged at their house.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanze, former chief clerk of the Protector-General, lodged at their house as a student.

sentences.zh: 雕武少美貌，為元則所愛悅，故偏被教。

translations.literal: Diaowu in youth was handsome and was loved and delighted in by Yuanze, so he received special instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in youth, Diaowu was favored by Yuanze and received special instruction.

sentences.zh: 因好學，精力絕人，負卷從師，不遠千里。

translations.literal: Because he loved learning, his energy surpassed others; bearing scrolls he followed teachers, not shunning a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, had exceptional energy, and traveled far to study under teachers.

sentences.zh: 遍通《五經》，尤明《三傳》。

translations.literal: He thoroughly mastered the Five Classics and was especially expert in the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics and was especially expert in the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 弟子遠方就業者，以百數，諸儒服其強辯。

translations.literal: Students who came from afar to study with him numbered in the hundreds; Confucians submitted to his forceful argumentation.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of students came from afar to study with him, and scholars respected his forceful argumentation.

sentences.zh: 齊神武召入霸府，令與諸子講說。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu summoned him into the Overlord’s Mansion and ordered him to lecture with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu summoned him to the Overlord’s Mansion to lecture with the princes.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，累遷平原太守，坐贓賄失官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Pingyuan, but lost office for bribery and corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianming he rose to Governor of Pingyuan but lost office for bribery.

sentences.zh: 武成即位，以舊恩，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Wucheng ascended, because of old favor he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Direct-and-Upright Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng ascended, he was made Regular Attendant of the Direct-and-Upright Cavalry for old favor.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王儼求博士，有司以雕武應選，時號得人。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Langye sought a doctor; the authorities nominated Diaowu for selection, and at the time he was praised as a good choice.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yan of Langye sought a doctor, the authorities nominated Diaowu, and he was praised as an excellent choice.

sentences.zh: 曆涇州刺史、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Jingzhou and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Jingzhou and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及帝侍講馬敬德卒，乃入授經書。

translations.literal: When the emperor's lecturer Ma Jingde died, he then entered to teach the classics.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Jingde died he taught the classics to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝甚重之，以為侍講，與侍書張景仁並被尊禮，同入華元殿，共讀《春秋》。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him, making him lecturer-in-attendance; together with Attendant Scribe Zhang Jingren he was honored, entering the Huayuan Hall to read the Spring and Autumn together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him lecturer with Zhang Jingren, reading the Spring and Autumn in the Huayuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 加國子祭酒、假儀同三司，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: He was additionally Libationer of the National University and Concurrent Equal to the Third Rank, awaiting orders at the Wulin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was Libationer and Concurrent Equal to the Third Rank at the Wulin Hall.

sentences.zh: 以景仁宗室，自托于其親何洪珍，公私之事，雕武常為其指南。

translations.literal: Because Jingren was of the imperial clan, he relied on his kinsman He Hongzhen; for public and private affairs Diaowu often served as his guide.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on He Hongzhen through Zhang Jingren's clan tie.

sentences.zh: 與張景仁號二張博士。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Jingren he was called the two Zhang doctors.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Jingren were called the two Zhang doctors.

sentences.zh: 時穆提婆、韓長鸞與洪珍同侍帷幄，知雕武為洪珍謀主，忌惡之。

translations.literal: At that time Muti Ba, Han Changluan, and Hongzhen together attended within the curtains; knowing Diaowu was Hongzhen's chief planner, they hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Muti Ba and Han Changluan hated him as Hongzhen's adviser.

sentences.zh: 洪珍又奏雕武監國史。

translations.literal: Hongzhen also memorialized that Diaowu supervise the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhen had him supervise historiography.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，加開府，奏度支事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and additionally Grand Guardian, memorializing on revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Attendant-in-Ordinary and oversaw revenue.

sentences.zh: 大被委任，言多見從，特敕奏事不趨，呼為博士。

translations.literal: Greatly entrusted, his words were often followed; specially ordered to memorialize without hurrying, he was called Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted his counsel and called him Doctor.

sentences.zh: 雕武自以出於微賤，致位大臣，勵精在公，有匪躬之節。

translations.literal: Diaowu, because he came from the lowest baseness to reach minister, strove in office with the spirit of not sparing his person.
translations.idiomatic: From humble origins he served zealously as minister.

sentences.zh: 議論無所回避，左右縱恣之徒，必加禁約。

translations.literal: In debate he did not avoid anything; toward the powerful who indulged themselves he always added prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked powerful favorites without fear.

sentences.zh: 數譏切寵要，獻替帷扆。

translations.literal: Several times he admonished favored intimates and offered corrections within the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly admonished court favorites.

sentences.zh: 帝亦深倚仗之，方委以朝政。

translations.literal: The emperor also deeply relied on him and was about to entrust court government to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nearly entrusted him with government.

sentences.zh: 雕武便以澂清為己任，意氣甚高。

translations.literal: Diaowu then took clarifying purity as his own task; his spirit was very high.
translations.idiomatic: He took purifying governance as his mission.

sentences.zh: 嘗在朝堂謂鄭子信曰：「向入省中，見賢家唐令處分，極無所以。

translations.literal: He once in the court hall told Zheng Zixin: "Just now entering the Secretariat I saw your family's Tang Ling's disposition—utterly without reason.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized a minister's conduct in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 若作數行兵帳，雕武不如邕；

translations.literal: If making several lines of military accounts, Diaowu is not equal to Yong;
translations.idiomatic: He said he was no clerk like Yong;

sentences.zh: 若致主堯、舜，身居稷、契，則邕不如我。」

translations.literal: if bringing the ruler to Yao and Shun and personally occupying the posts of Ji and Qi, then Yong is not equal to me.
translations.idiomatic: but he could guide the ruler like the ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 長鸞等陰圖之。

translations.literal: Changluan and others plotted against him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 及與侍中崔季舒、黃門侍郎郭遵諫幸晉陽，為長鸞所譖，誅。

translations.literal: Together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Jishu and Yellow Gate Gentleman Guo Zun he remonstrated against the imperial visit to Jinyang and was slandered by Changluan and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed for remonstrating against the Jinyang journey.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，帝使段孝言詰之。

translations.literal: Facing execution, the emperor sent Duan Xiaoyan to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Duan Xiaoyan to question him before execution.

sentences.zh: 雕武曰：「臣起自諸生，光寵隆洽。

translations.literal: Diaowu said: "Your servant rose from the various students to splendid favor overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Diaowu said he rose from scholarship to favor.

sentences.zh: 今者之諫，臣實首謀，意善功惡，無所逃死。

translations.literal: Today's remonstrance—your servant was truly the chief planner; the intent was good though the achievement evil; there is no escaping death.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted death for his remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 願陛下珍愛金玉，開發神明，數引賈誼之倫，語其政道，令聽覽之間，無所擁蔽，則臣雖死，猶生之年。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to treasure gold and jade, open and develop divine clarity, and several times bring men like Jia Yi to speak of governance so that between listening and viewing nothing is blocked—then though your servant dies, it is still the years of life.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to heed worthy advisers even as he died.

sentences.zh: 因歔欷流涕，俯而就戮。

translations.literal: He then sighed and wept, bowed his head and went to execution.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and went to the block.

sentences.zh: 左右莫不憐而壯之。

translations.literal: Those left and right all pitied and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers pitied and admired him.

sentences.zh: 子德沖等徙北邊。

translations.literal: His son Dechong and others were moved to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dechong was exiled north.

sentences.zh: 南安王思好之反，德沖及弟德揭俱免。

translations.literal: When Prince Sihao of Nan'an rebelled, Dechong and his younger brother Dejie were both pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: They were pardoned after Sihao's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 德沖聰敏好學，以帝師之子，早見旌擢，位中書舍人。

translations.literal: Dechong was clever, loved learning, and as the emperor's teacher's son was early honored and promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Dechong rose to Secretariat Gentleman as the lecturer's son.

sentences.zh: 其父之戮，德沖並在殿廷就執，目見冤酷，號哭，殞絕於地，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: At his father's execution Dechong was seized in the hall courtyard; he saw the cruel injustice, cried out, and collapsed on the ground, long unconscious before reviving.
translations.idiomatic: He witnessed his father's execution and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 郭遵者，钜鹿人也。

translations.literal: Guo Zun was a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zun was from Julu.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣為太原公時，為國常侍。

translations.literal: When Qi Wenxuan was Prince of Taiyuan he was Regular Attendant of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan was Prince of Taiyuan, Zun was state regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝家人有蓋豐洛者，典知家務，號曰蓋將。

translations.literal: Among the emperor's household was Gai Fengluo who managed household affairs, called General Gai.
translations.idiomatic: The household manager Gai Fengluo was called General Gai.

sentences.zh: 遵因其處分，曾抗拒，為高德正所貴。

translations.literal: Zun once resisted his disposition and was valued by Gao Dezheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zun once defied Gai and was valued by Gao Dezheng.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，由是擢為主書，專令訪察。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, because of this he was promoted chief scribe with special charge to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's founding he became chief investigator.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人硃謂為钜鹿太守，遵為弟子求官，謂啟文宣，鞭之二百，付京畿。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Zhu Wei was made governor of Julu; Zun sought office for his disciple, told Wenxuan, and was flogged two hundred strokes and handed to the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: He was flogged for seeking favor for a disciple.

sentences.zh: 久之，除並省尚書都令史、建州別駕。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Chief Clerk of the combined ministries and Military Administrator of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became chief clerk and military administrator.

sentences.zh: 會韓長鸞父永興為刺史，因此遂相參附。

translations.literal: When Han Changluan's father Yongxing was governor, because of this they became mutually attached.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Han Changluan's father.

sentences.zh: 後擢為黃門侍郎，被誅。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted Yellow Gate Gentleman and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Yellow Gate Gentleman and was executed.

sentences.zh: 遵出自賤微，易為盈滿。

translations.literal: Zun came from the lowest baseness and easily became full to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: From the lowest origins he grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 宮門逢諸貴，輒呼姓字，語言佈置，極為輕率。

translations.literal: Meeting the noble at palace gates he would call their names and arrange speech, extremely rash.
translations.idiomatic: He addressed nobles by name at the gates.

sentences.zh: 嘗于宮門牽韓長鸞，辭曰：「王在得言。

translations.literal: He once at the palace gate pulled Han Changluan, saying: "The king may speak freely.
translations.idiomatic: He grabbed Changluan and said the king should speak freely.

sentences.zh: 主上縱放如此，曾不規諫，何名大臣？」

translations.literal: The sovereign indulges thus and never remonstrates—what name is there for great minister?
translations.idiomatic: He accused Changluan of failing to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 長鸞嫌其率爾，便掣手而去，由是不加援，故及於禍。

translations.literal: Changluan disliked his rashness, pulled his hand away and left; because of this he gave no support, and therefore he met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan withdrew support and he met disaster.
